articles.title: How AI Is Changing the Pace of Discovery for Millions Living With Dementia
articles.summary:
There are 57 million people worldwide living with dementia today. For the researchers working to help them, the obstacle isn’t a lack of effort — it’s too much data, too few experts to synthesize it and a pace of discovery that can’t keep up with the disease.
The Consortium for Biomedical Research and AI in Neurodegeneration (C-BRAIN), working with NVIDIA, is using AI to change that.
Alzheimer’s disease is one of today’s leading global health challenges, with over 10 million new dementia cases diagnosed each year. Despite a 7x increase in National Institutes of Health funding in the last 15 years — reaching $3.9 billion annually — no treatment has been found to stop, prevent or reverse the disease yet.
The bottlenecks are not enough high impact scientific findings, too much data living in institutional silos and too slow a pace of synthesis to keep up with the research that is published.
C-BRAIN, led by Dr. Randall Bateman and a consortium of 18 member institutions across academic, philanthropic, pharma and research organizations, launched in November 2025 to help scientists make better, faster discoveries by accelerating the research that makes new treatments possible.
“We have a window of opportunity with artificial intelligence to do research fundamentally different than we’ve ever done before, in a way that accelerates discoveries to help patients,” said Bateman, founder and director of C-BRAIN and the Charles F. and Joanne Knight Distinguished Professor of Neurology at t…

articles.title: Tailscale Rushes Patches After Uncoordinated Disclosure of ‘Tailworm’ Flaws
articles.summary:
Tailscale is getting ready to ship a client update that addresses privilege escalation weaknesses in Tailscale SSH. Details of the bugs went public over the weekend.
Tailscale provides a mesh VPN service that uses the WireGuard protocol to connect an organization’s devices and services over a private, peer-to-peer network.
The Tailscale vulnerabilities, dubbed Tailworm, are described in a report from Cyberdione Labs. It lists 11 findings affecting version 1.104.2 of the Tailscale client and version 0.29.5 of headscale, an open source control server that organizations can host themselves.
Cyberdione Labs published the report before any patches were available, drawing criticism on social media, though the researchers argued that rapid awareness would speed up remediation.
Six of the findings are rated high severity, and four of them concern Tailscale SSH, which grants access based on device identity and network policy instead of passwords or keys.
According to the Tailworm report, Tailscale SSH performs some forwarding operations with root privileges, and the safeguards meant to restrict them can be bypassed.
An attacker who has compromised one device could exploit this against any server that device is permitted to reach over Tailscale SSH, as long as the access rule allows forwarding. In lab tests, this resulted in root access on target servers and the theft of keys that can be used to add rogue devices to the network.

articles.title: Smart Window adds new form filling and page watching features | The Mozilla Blog
articles.summary:
Skip the busywork with Smart Window
The days might be getting shorter, but your to-do list is only getting longer. Whether you’re getting a head start on holiday shopping or planning your next career move, Smart Window’s newest features will help you keep up.
Firefox’s opt-in AI browsing experience can now use information from tabs you choose to help fill out forms. It can also watch web pages and notify you about specific changes you’ve asked it to track.
Let your open tabs fill in the blanks
Job applications ask for your work history; event registrations ask for a professional bio. If those details are already in your open tabs, Smart Window can now use pages you choose to suggest what to enter, saving you extra clicks and some Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V.
For example, Smart Window could use information from your online portfolio or professional profile to fill in your work history, or draw on those details to draft an answer to a question like “Tell me about a time when…” Firefox’s regular autofill still handles saved information such as your name and address, which can be entered directly into forms without relying on AI models.
To get started, click into a form field. If the form has at least four text fields that Smart Window can help fill, you’ll see “Fill from sources” appear in the dropdown, along with a recommended source page. articles.title: Ford Fathom will be the cheapest American EV capable of powering a house | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Ford announced two new EV chargers today that will allow its forthcoming Fathom pickup truck to serve as a battery capable of delivering power to the home or grid.
The new chargers promise to be about half the cost of Ford’s existing equivalent products, which could make the technology available to more households. Ford said the Fathom itself will start at $28,350.
The Fathom will be capable of delivering “over 10 kW” to a home, Ford said. That would allow the electric vehicle to substitute for a small standby generator. For most U.S. homes, it wouldn’t be enough to power everything, but it could keep a refrigerator and air conditioner operational for about half a day.
Such capability has been touted as an advantage EVs have over fossil fuel vehicles, but not many EVs come properly equipped, and the chargers required to make use of vehicle-to-everything (V2X) services tend to be costly.
Ford’s two devices offer similar but differing capabilities.
The Home Power Station device can help customers shave their utility bill by charging the Fathom when power prices are low and sending electricity back to the home when prices are high. The automaker says it will cost around $650, about 50% less than its first-generation bidirectional charger.

A decisão ocorre enquanto a montadora tenta recuperar espaço na China. articles.title: 100 nanomètres, 700 fois plus fine qu'un cheveu : le rover Perseverance mesure le danger invisible de la poussière martienne
articles.summary:
100 nanomètres, 700 fois plus fine qu'un cheveu : le rover Perseverance mesure le danger invisible de la poussière martienne
L'humanité ambitionne de conquérir un jour la planète rouge. Pourtant, un ennemi aussi discret que redoutable se dresse sur le chemin des futurs explorateurs : la poussière martienne. Actuellement sur le terrain, le rover Perseverance fournit à la NASA des données cruciales pour concevoir et protéger les futures combinaisons et les habitats spatiaux.
Marcher sur la planète Mars constitue un défi encore plus colossal pour notre époque que ne le fut la conquête de la Lune à la fin des années 1960. Le challenge s'annonce presque impossible, tant les obstacles techniques et biologiques à surmonter s'avèrent titanesques.
La NASA, titillée par Elon Musk, croit toutefois dur comme fer à ce voyage habité et s'emploie à lever les barrières l'une après l'autre. Après les récentes annonces concernant un démonstrateur de vaisseau à propulsion nucléaire prévu pour 2028, l'agence spatiale étasunienne s'attaque aujourd'hui à un problème très concret : la survie des futurs “marswalkers”. Celles et ceux qui, à leurs risques et périls, fouleront le sol de notre voisine devront en effet affronter une menace littéralement invisible.

articles.title: L’application LCL est en panne ce mercredi matin : les signalements se multiplient
articles.summary:
Les clients de LCL qui ont tenté de consulter leurs comptes ce mercredi 28 octobre 2026 ont eu une mauvaise surprise.
Depuis le début de la matinée, l’application mobile de la banque rencontre des dysfonctionnements, et de nombreux utilisateurs se plaignent de ne pas pouvoir y accéder normalement.
Une hausse des signalements sur Downdetector
L’ampleur du problème se lit sur Downdetector, où les signalements concernant LCL grimpent depuis ce matin, signe que la panne ne se limite pas à quelques cas isolés et touche un nombre important de clients.
Selon nos observations, l’accès aux comptes via l’application et via le site web est concerné.
Pour l’heure, LCL ne s’est pas exprimée sur l’origine de l’incident ni sur le délai nécessaire pour rétablir le service. Rien à signaler en revanche du côté du Crédit Agricole, qui appartient pourtant au même groupe.

articles.title: OpenAI lanzó GPT-6.1 Terra, un modelo de IA que usa la computadora y cuesta la mitad
articles.summary:
OpenAI lanzó el 26 de octubre GPT-6.1 Terra, un modelo de inteligencia artificial de gama media pensado para trabajo de oficina en la computadora. Sus precios para desarrolladores son un 50% menores que los de GPT-5.6 Terra, su antecesor, y los de GPT-6.1 Sol, un modelo superior de la misma empresa.
Según el anuncio de la compañía, Terra combina razonamiento visual, uso preciso de la computadora y una redacción más natural. Entre las tareas que menciona están redactar propuestas, interpretar planos técnicos, completar formularios y editar videos.
Ya está disponible para los usuarios de los planes Plus, Pro, Enterprise y Edu en ChatGPT Work y en Codex, la herramienta de programación de OpenAI. Los desarrolladores pueden usarlo en la API (la conexión para integrarlo en otras aplicaciones) con el nombre gpt-6.1-terra. El anuncio no menciona el plan gratuito.
USD 1 por millón de unidades de texto de entrada
El precio estándar es de USD 1 por millón de tokens de entrada y USD 5 por millón de salida, según la documentación oficial. Los tokens son las unidades de texto que procesa y cobra un modelo. La firma Artificial Analysis, que mide modelos de IA, informó que GPT-5.6 Terra costaba USD 2 y USD 12, respectivamente.
El modelo acepta texto e imágenes, y responde solo con texto. Tiene una ventana de contexto de 1.050.000 tokens, es decir, la cantidad de información que puede manejar en una sola consulta, y su conocimiento llega hasta el 1 de junio de 2026.

articles.title: CISA confirms PHP2Shell vulnerabilities now exploited in attacks
articles.summary:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added two critical PHP vulnerabilities collectively tracked as PHP2Shell to its catalog of actively exploited security flaws.
Threat actors without privileges can exploit the two security issues (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) in high-complexity attacks to gain remote code execution (RCE) on unpatched systems.
The PHP security team patched the two flaws on Wednesday, October 21, one day after urging security teams to install the security updates as soon as they became available.
Although details on the PHP2Shell security flaws (including the CVE IDs and mitigation measures shared with critical infrastructure providers) leaked and some proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits were published online before patches went live, the PHP security team said that none were functional.
Multiple cybersecurity firms (including Cloudflare, Amazon, Hadrian, watchTowr, Previdian, and Patchstack) also detected widespread exploitation attempts before public disclosure, but they all tagged them as unsuccessful.
Amazon Threat Intelligence security researchers also said that attackers began targeting the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities four days before security patches were released.
Federal agencies ordered to patch by Thursday

articles.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
articles.summary:
Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. articles.title: CISA Warns of Node2Shell Exploitation as Honeypots Log Attack Attempts
articles.summary:
The US cybersecurity agency CISA has added the Brotli vulnerability known as Node2Shell to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. Separately, two security firms say they have recorded exploitation attempts against their honeypots.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111497 and also known as HTTP2Shell and Broccoli2Shell, the flaw is an out-of-bounds write in the decoder of Brotli, the data compression library developed by Google.
It impacts Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0. With specially crafted compressed data, an attacker could crash the application, expose the contents of its memory, and potentially execute arbitrary code.
The bug was reported by researchers at OpenAI, and Node.js and Google released fixes on October 21. Microsoft, the maintainers of two Python packages, Bun, Envoy and Istio have also released fixes, and Palo Alto Networks is rolling out hotfixes for PAN-OS.
Imperva has demonstrated that the vulnerability can be exploited for code execution on an official Node.js image.
CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to the KEV catalog on October 27, but provided no information on the attacks. Federal civilian agencies have been instructed to address the flaw by November 10.
Previdian, which monitors exploitation activity through its own network of sensors, says it recorded one exploitation attempt targeting CVE-2026-111497 on October 27, coming from a US-based IP address. The company rates its confidence in the exploitation as ‘confirmed’.

articles.title: 3 Ways to Boost MoE Inference on NVIDIA DGX Spark | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Generating tokens faster starts with identifying what limits inference performance. In the batch-size-1 evaluation of Ling-3.0-flash from Inclusion AI on NVIDIA DGX Spark, profiling showed that decoding was memory-bound: reading model weights drove execution time. Two operations stood out—the mixture-of-experts (MoE) computation and the output-layer projection that produces scores across the model’s vocabulary.
Those findings pointed to two ways to improve performance: reduce the weight traffic in each decode step and generate more tokens per verification round. This post examines three techniques that address those costs:
- Humming MXFP4 MoE kernels to improve execution of the routed-expert computation.
- Online FP8 quantization of the output layer, or LM head, to reduce its weight-read volume.
- Multi-token prediction (MTP) speculative decoding with NEXTN to draft and verify multiple tokens together.
This post explains how each optimization works, measures its effect, and examines an integration issue that can make the combined configuration slower than the baseline. Ling-3.0-flash serves as the implementation example, with code and deployment instructions in the Ling cookbook.
Model and baseline configuration
The evaluation used Ling-3.0-flash-fp4, a mixture-of-experts model with 124 billion total parameters and 5.1 billion active parameters per token. The model has 42 layers: 35 Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) linear-attention layers and seven multi-head latent attention (MLA)…

articles.title: I Tried to Fool a Scientific Publisher With AI
articles.summary:
I Used AI to Fake a Scientific Paper. Here’s What Happened
My experiment with an IEEE journal revealed AI’s threats to scholarly publishing
Science has a spam problem. And the spam filter is getting clogged up.
According to all reports, academic publishing is drowning in what has come to be called AI slop: low-quality, mass-produced content generated with AI. By 2025, an estimated 57 percent of all published academic articles exhibited detectable evidence of large language model (LLM) influence, a massive jump from 12 percent in 2023. What’s more, over 12 percent of Nature Communications reviews were found to be completely AI-generated in 2025.
Given that for every 40 papers showing statistical evidence of AI usage in 2025, only one formally disclosed it, these figures likely grossly underestimate LLM involvement today. Of course, evidence of AI use doesn’t necessarily mean a paper is slop. But some estimates suggest that hundreds of thousands of fake, often AI-generated, publications are now produced annually.
“It’s not just the [scientific] record under threat, it’s science as a whole,” warns Amanda Sulicz, IEEE’s research-integrity manager. “AI slop is completely eroding trust in science and every scientific process that we’ve worked for centuries to create.”
Yet statistics and statements claiming that the problem is big—perhaps even existential for science—don’t really get the message across. Just how easy is it to use AI to create a convincing but completely fake paper? …

- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.

Threat actors have started probing for a newly patched critical vulnerability in Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS), threat intelligence firm Defused reports.
The exploited flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-101767 (CVSS score of 9.8), was patched last week in Oracle’s October CPU.
It is described as an SQL injection issue in the Application Object Library product of EBS that could be exploited by remote, unauthenticated attackers over HTTP.
Successful exploitation of the bug could allow attackers to achieve remote code execution (RCE) and completely take over the Application Object Library.
According to Defused, the first exploitation attempts targeting CVE-2026-101767 were observed on October 27.
“Our Oracle E-Business Suite decoys recorded exploratory exploits against CVE-2026-101767 this morning, Oct 27,” the company warned on X.
The security defect was discovered and reported by Horizon3.ai and there have been no other reports regarding its in-the-wild exploitation.
Oracle EBS vulnerabilities are often targeted by threat actors. In June, Defused warned of attacks exploiting CVE-2026-46817, a critical issue in the File Transmissions component of E-Business Suite’s Payments product.
Last year, the Cl0p ransomware and extortion group exploited zero-day bugs in Oracle’s enterprise management software to access stored data.

Post-training can adapt an open model to these needs. With suitable data and evaluation, it can improve accuracy and usefulness while supporting safer interactions with the model. This gives countries and industries greater control over how their agents reflect local priorities and serve the people who use them.
NVIDIA built Nemotron-Personas-France with French AI startup Pleias, and Nemotron-Personas-Belgium with Pleias and Belgian university KU Leuven. Both are part of the open NVIDIA Nemotron data program, which includes locale-grounded persona datasets for 12 countries that developers can use to adapt open models market by market.
In this blog, we will discuss how to take Nemotron open models and post-train them with Nemotron datasets to tailor them for regional languages and cultures.
The difference post-training makes

articles.title: The imec Report: Scaling Optical Interconnects For The AI Era
articles.summary:
Unprecedented demand for bandwidth calls for bringing optics closer to silicon through a fundamental rethinking of the optical interconnect roadmap.
The explosive growth of cloud computing and AI – from generative, and reasoning, to (ultimately) agentic systems – is creating unprecedented demand for bandwidth, as the amount of data that must be moved both within and between data centers continues to surge. In turn, this exposes growing limitations in the underlying interconnects that not only span the data center fabric and rack level but also extend deep inside servers – down to where they link XPUs, memory, and other system components at the package and die level.
Copper-based (electrical) interconnects have long been the industry’s workhorse thanks to their low cost, simplicity, and reliability. Yet today, they are increasingly hitting fundamental limits: while highly energy-efficient electrical links can be realized, they are typically confined to very short reaches (on the order of millimeters). At longer distances and higher lane rates, power consumption rises sharply, thermal constraints intensify, and signal integrity degrades. In other words, electrical I/O is rapidly becoming a key barrier to scaling next-generation AI and machine learning systems.
Optical interconnects have emerged as a critical path forward. By transmitting data using light rather than electrical signals, they are far less sensitive to distance, enabling much better energy efficiency while mitigat…

A mobile robot slows for someone in a hallway. A collaborative arm eases its movement as a worker approaches. A humanoid pauses to let a person pass. Each response depends on information about the robot or its surroundings: a distance reading, a position estimate, or a stop signal.
But what happens when one of those inputs is wrong, and the robot still responds exactly as designed? The mobile robot reads the hallway as clear while someone is still there. The arm estimates that the worker is farther away. The humanoid does not receive a stop signal as a person crosses its path.
In each case, a fault could cause that mismatch. So could deliberate manipulation.

Two Democratic senators who have long overseen US intelligence say the Trump administration is illegally withholding a secret court’s findings from Congress until lawmakers renew a program that lets federal agents read Americans’ communications without a warrant.
Seven months ago, the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court objected to search filters that let intelligence analysts pull Americans’ messages from intercepted data without the approvals, written justifications, or records the law requires. The court approved another year of surveillance anyway. The ruling has never been made public, and Senators Ron Wyden of Oregon and Adam Schiff of California say the administration’s own deadline for releasing it passed in September.
The program, Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA), lapsed in June after Congress failed to renew it, though collection continues under the court’s March approval. The administration’s own public documentation says rulings like this one are reviewed for public release “within 180 days of issuance.” That window closed September 13, even as intelligence officials press lawmakers to reauthorize the program by the end of the year.

Sin respuesta. La cantidad es pequeña, sí, pero cuando se trata de una administración pública, tirar del BOE para notificar a alguien es un recurso obligatorio para que el procedimiento pueda continuar a la vez que se le sigue dando a la persona la oportunidad de responder. Ocurre igual en muchos otras situaciones, como cuando se impone una multa de tráfico a alguien y no se le puede localizar.
Qué ha pasado. Según el aviso, publicado el 24 de septiembre y firmado por el jefe de personal del ayuntamiento, se le pagaron al trabajador varios días en los que no se presentó y no dio ninguna justificación. El ayuntamiento califica dichos salarios como pagos indebidos y ha abierto un expediente para recuperarlos. Desde el medio local Burgos Conecta informan de que los intentos del ayuntamiento por entregar la notificación en su domicilio habían fracasado. El anuncio del BOE no menciona el nombre del empleado ni indica qué días estuvieron implicados.

In the cockpit of Beta Technologies’ Alia CX300, pilot Chris Caputo steers onto Runway 33 at Patrick Leahy Burlington International Airport in Vermont. Cleared for takeoff, he releases the brakes and nudges the throttle forward.
At the back of the aircraft, the five-blade pusher propeller snaps awake, and the Alia bolts forward. There’s no shriek of a turbofan spooling up, no shudder of a piston engine, and no wait for thrust. Just the low hum of an electric motor and a shove of instant acceleration.
Within a few seconds, we’re at 85 knots (almost 160 kilometers per hour), and Caputo rotates the nose upward. The runway drops abruptly away as we climb. Gaining speed and altitude, we head northwest over Lake Champlain. Through the wraparound canopy, I watch the hunched shoulders of Vermont’s Green Mountains shrink under the right wing, with New York’s taller Adirondacks to the left.

The machine, he says, is much simpler to manage than the Cessna 182 I flew around Australia in my student-pilot days.

articles.title: Apple backports CoreGraphics zero-day patches to older iPhones

Apple has backported security patches released last month to older iPhones and iPads, addressing a zero-day bug exploited in "extremely sophisticated" targeted attacks on iOS devices.
Apple patched the same vulnerability in September for devices running iOS 26.7.1 and iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1.
Meta Product Security discovered this out-of-bounds write weakness (tracked as CVE-2026-86950) in CoreGraphics, a framework used for two-dimensional vector graphics, text drawing, and image rendering across iOS, macOS, iPadOS, watchOS, and tvOS.
Successful exploitation of out-of-bounds write security issues can let attackers crash programs, corrupt data, or gain remote code execution by writing data outside the allocated memory buffer.
"Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals on versions of iOS before iOS 27," Apple warned on Monday.
"Processing a maliciously crafted file may lead to arbitrary code execution. An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved bounds checking."
With this week's security patches, Apple has now also addressed this vulnerability on iPhone XS, iPhone XS Max, iPhone XR, iPad 7th generation, iPad Air 4th generation and later, iPad 9th generation and later, and iPad mini 6th generation and later.

How solid-state transformers could help power the AI boom
New technology could help cut power losses and reinvent a staple of the grid.
Transformers are a crucial but nearly invisible part of our grid. The devices help efficiently move power across long distances, but they’re complicated and in short supply. And given that their basic design hasn’t changed much for about a century, they could use an upgrade.
As the world races to meet rising electricity demand from EVs, data centers, and more, researchers and companies are looking to modernize transformers. New, solid-state versions could help relieve some of the supply concerns and make sure the grid can handle the growing pressure.
Conventional transformers generally rely on huge amounts of specialized steel alloys and miles of copper wire to do their work of transferring electricity between circuits. Solid-state models, in comparison, combine magnetic components with high-power semiconductors, making them more compact and allowing for more control over the flow of electricity.
These devices are still in development, and can’t replace all traditional transformers today, especially the largest ones that work at the high voltages necessary for long-distance transmission. But a new generation of transformer technology could be a crucial part of our future grid.

articles.title: Sculpture re-creates odd optical effects of famed Lycurgus Cup
articles.summary:
Dating back to around 400 CE and made of dichroic glass, the Lycurgus Cup is notable for exhibiting different colors depending on the light. (It gets its name from the scene depicted on its surface, of King Lycurgus of Thrace.) Light it from the front, and the cup looks green; light it from behind, and the color changes to a deep red. University of Sheffield scientists have re-created the original recipe to produce a contemporary glass sculpture with the same optical effect.
The cup is considered one of the seven glass wonders of the world, one of just 40 glass cage cups that survived. Exactly why the unusual color effects of the Lycurgus Cup occurred was a mystery until 2007, when a team of scientists discovered the color shifts were due to the presence of nanoparticles in the glass—the result of Roman artisans adding finely ground gold and silver into the mix. Those nanoparticles change how the electrons in the cup vibrate in response to light so that the color one sees shifts with the observer’s vantage point.
As we reported in 2019, it’s a similar phenomenon to the one responsible for the shifting colors of 19th-century daguerreotypes due to the scattering properties of nanoparticles. The Romans added salt when they melted the silicon (sand) to make the glass, and those salts contained gold atoms. articles.title: Memory-Enforced GPU Sharing in Kubernetes with NVIDIA CUDA 13.4 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Many AI workloads need only a fraction of a GPU. Giving each one an entire device can leave capacity idle; sharing GPUs lets platform teams serve more workloads with the infrastructure they already have.
NVIDIA GPUs already support several approaches to sharing. Multi-instance GPU (MIG) splits a GPU into hardware-isolated instances that are transparent to the application, time-slicing lets several processes take turns without memory enforcement, and Multi-Process Service (MPS) lets them run concurrently in separate address spaces (sm-sharing).
CUDA 13.4 now enforces a memory boundary that is transparent to the application with a new time-sharing mode, alongside the compute sharing mode (sm-sharing) that already existed in MPS.
Here is what the CUDA release brings:
- An exact memory amount: A workload asks for a memory size and CUDA holds it there. An allocation above that size fails, just as it would on a smaller GPU.
- A range: A workload gets a guaranteed minimum plus a maximum it can grow into when memory is free.
- A compute mode: Each workload can choose to use its compute in an sm-sharing mode rather than using the default time-sharing mode.
- A transparent memory limit: Each workload sees only a fraction of the GPU memory.

articles.title: Atomic-6 ha mandado su armadura para satélites al espacio y reza para que reciba un impacto

La basura espacial es un problema por muchos motivos. Uno de ellos es la posibilidad de que algún fragmento de chatarra impacte con un satélite y lo destroce o afecte a su funcionamiento. Otro es la generación del temido síndrome del Kessler, según el cual un fragmento de basura espacial puede generar más fragmentos al impactar, provocando un peligroso efecto dominó. Existen escudos que protegen a los satélites del impacto de chatarra, pero en el proceso se generan más fragmentos, por lo que se potencia el segundo inconveniente. Por eso, la startup Atomic-6 ha desarrollado Space Armor, una armadura diseñada para acabar con ambos problemas de un plumazo.
Un prototipo en el espacio. Atomic-6 ha enviado su primer prototipo de Space Armor en la nave Starburst-1 de Portal Space Systems, a bordo de un cohete Falcon 9 de SpaceX. Los ingenieros de la compañía esperan que en el tiempo que esté en el espacio reciba algún impacto de estos fragmentos diminutos, de modo que puedan detectar mediante telemetría cómo se comporta el escudo.
El gran problema. Los fragmentos grandes de basura espacial se pueden detectar, de modo que las colisiones con ellas sean prevenibles. Sin embargo, la mayor parte de esta chatarra es muy pequeña y difícilmente rastreable. Según una estimación de la ESA, en el espacio hay más de 65.000 objetos mayores de 10 cm, en torno a 1,5 millones entre 1 y 10 cm y unos 230 millones entre 1 mm y 1 cm. Estas son cifras que, además, van aumentando rápidamente.

articles.title: One pod, one node: The architecture behind serverless Kubernetes on AWS
articles.summary:
One pod, one node: The architecture behind serverless Kubernetes on AWS
A pod-level walkthrough of admission routing, dedicated scheduling, and network isolation, no worker nodes required
Serverless Kubernetes changes who manages the node, not what Kubernetes expects from it. Kubernetes expects a node to register with the control plane, report capacity, run a Kubelet, provide networking, and host workloads. AWS Fargate provides those behaviors without asking customers to create, patch, scale, or replace a fleet of worker nodes.
Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) Fargate solves that problem by making the pod the unit of infrastructure. When a pod is selected for Fargate, EKS provisions a dedicated compute environment, boots the Kubernetes components it needs, gives the pod an Elastic Network Interface (ENI) in the customer’s virtual private cloud (VPC), and tears the environment down when the pod is gone.
“Serverless Kubernetes changes who manages the node, not what Kubernetes expects from it.”
That customer experience depends on several coordinated design choices. Admission-time routing prevents the default scheduler from claiming a Fargate pod. A Fargate-specific scheduler provisions capacity instead of selecting from a pre-existing node pool. A focused runtime image supplies the Kubernetes node components, while separate network namespaces keep the platform path distinct from the workload path. Living digital twins are helping industrial plants run more like living systems, and setting the stage for industries that work in sync.
Most people associate industrial environments with cold steel and clockwork machinery. Functionally, though, a plant or factory is more like a living thing: It has a pulse, even a metabolism. It goes through wear and tear as it ages, and signs of deteriorating health often show up as barely perceptible irregularities.
Digital twin technology has long aimed to mirror that dynamism and model anomalies that may be symptomatic of larger problems. But earlier implementations were a few beats behind physical reality; they were incapable of real-time analysis and unable to proactively address any issues detected. They focused more on simulation, observation and what-if scenario planning, rather than closed-loop execution. Rather than serving as a digital mirror of reality that can spot anomalies or suggest optimizations, a living digital twin combines a dynamic, high-fidelity digital representation of complex operations with the capacity to intervene in the physical world through operations and control systems.

articles.title: Hiding Capabilities in AI Models - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
Hiding Capabilities in AI Models
Interesting research: “AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities”
Abstract: Capability evaluations aim to surface dangerous model behaviors before deployment, but their reliability depends on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be elicited. We show this assumption does not hold under adversarial conditions by constructing backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within host model weights, decrypting and executing them only upon receiving a secret trigger. Using digital lockers, these hidden circuits remain provably hard to elicit and interpret under cryptographic assumptions, even given full access to model weights, extending prior work from hiding fixed strings to arbitrary computations. We implement our proof of concept constructions in PyTorch and evaluate elicitation through fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training, using a small chemical reaction prediction task as a proxy for CBRN-relevant capabilities. Our results demonstrate resistance to these methods and, together with our cryptographic guarantees, reveal a limit of elicitation-based capability audits. We release our models to support the improvement of defenses.

articles.title: Announcing SOCI-indexed images for faster SageMaker AI jobs | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Announcing SOCI-indexed images for faster SageMaker AI jobs
Every minute your deep learning container image spends downloading is a minute you pay for and a minute your team waits. Container image download is pure overhead: billable job time that produces no model progress. For modern deep learning images, that overhead is several minutes on every single job. Today, we’re excited to announce Seekable OCI (SOCI) indexing for Amazon SageMaker AI Training and Amazon SageMaker AI processing jobs, which takes full container image download off the critical path of every job.
With SOCI indexing, SageMaker AI lazy-loads your container image. It fetches only the files needed to start the container and streams the rest in the background as your code runs, so your job begins in seconds instead of minutes. You adopt it by pointing to a pre-indexed AWS Deep Learning Container (DLC) or adding an index to your own image. Neither approach requires changes to your job definition, entry point, or data channels. The result is faster job starts, lower job cost, and more time spent building models rather than waiting on infrastructure.
SOCI-indexed images start Amazon SageMaker AI training containers in seconds, with no impact on training performance. As we show in the What we measured section, this reduced GPU idle time during image pulls by up to 90 percent in our benchmarks.

articles.title: When “isolated” doesn’t mean isolated: How to sandbox AI agents
articles.summary:
When “isolated” doesn’t mean isolated: How to sandbox AI agents
Separation of workloads before AI wasn’t easy, but it was far more straightforward. Servers sat in data centers, VLANs segregated packets, firewall rules managed ingress/egress, and physical cables separated packets to and from their destinations.
Now, flip on an agent, and it has access to almost everything by default.
Enterprises cannot operate with that default, and in this article, you’ll learn how to implement true sandboxing at every layer that matters.
Why aren’t containers enough to sandbox AI agents?
When you run a container (think Docker), it’s a lightweight package that runs as an isolated process. But that isolation has limits. Containers share the host kernel, and those on Docker’s default bridge can communicate with one another. A container cannot directly access host files by default, but a writable bind mount can let it modify or delete the host files exposed through that mount.
If you rely on a container alone for agent isolation, you may leave important boundaries unprotected. Thinking of containers as locked down by default is a major security risk. When running workloads in Kubernetes, you have tools like NetworkPolicy, service mesh for secure service communication, and SecurityContext to ensure containers run in a governed way.

Eso y que, por primera vez, tenemos que ampliar el eje hasta los cuatro grados de anomalía para que no se salga por arriba.
¿Qué es exactamente El Niño? No está de más recordar que nos referimos a un fenómeno climático cíclico (aunque muy irregular) que tiene grandes efectos sobre el clima mundial. Enormes, de hecho. Si excluimos a las estaciones, se trata de la fuente más importante de variabilidad climática anual de todo el planeta.
Durante la fase cálida (es decir, durante El Niño), la ausencia de unos vientos alíseos fuertes que refresquen la superficie del Pacífico ecuatorial hace que la temperatura de esa zona del océano se dispare. Los efectos son variados y cambian según la región ("condiciones más secas de lo normal en determinadas partes del mundo; mientras que en otras provoca más precipitaciones. Cómo se encontraron las nuevas soluciones
La investigación que se publicó en arXiv es el resultado del esfuerzo conjunto de Opal Issan, Jonathan Citrin, Matt Landreman y Brendan Tracey. Los autores generalizaron las dos familias de soluciones anteriores mediante un parámetro en cada una, que rompe la simetría de stellarator. Los stellarators son dispositivos de fusión que utilizan campos magnéticos tridimensionales para contener el plasma.
Con el fin de encontrar generalizaciones de las familias de soluciones conocidas, los autores entregaron la investigación de Landreman y sus preguntas abiertas a un pequeño equipo de agentes de Gemini 4 en Google Antigravity. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. But advanced packaging is making that separation much harder to maintain.
For years, engineers moved much of what they needed between companies through datasheets, design rules, and qualification specs, while the manufacturing knowledge stayed with the supplier. That arrangement held as long as the pieces behaved independently, but what one company keeps inside its process now shapes how another company’s part of the package performs once everything is assembled. The process may still belong to the supplier, but its consequences no longer end at the factory gate.

Amazon swapped its usual big fall hardware showcase this year for a series of smaller launches throughout October. So far this month, it has announced new Fire TV devices, new Kindles, the Alexa Tablet Pro 12, Ring’s first smart lock, new hardware from AI-wearable startup Bee, and new Blink 4K cameras.
Inside Amazon’s Echo hardware event
The company’s low-key product launch was designed to give each device more attention, according to Panos Panay.
Then this week, it hosted journalists at a small event in New York City’s financial district to showcase its new Echo hardware.
Panos Panay, senior vice president of devices, Alexa, and Leo at Amazon, kicked off proceedings by explaining the company’s approach this year. “We have so many products we’re launching that are meaningful,” he said. “However, we get to this point when we do everything at once; not all your children get enough attention.” This longer rollout allows for more focus on each launch. He also teased two more launches still to come — from Ring and some “Echo on the Go” news — before explaining that today’s focus is “the most important focus we have, which is the home.”
He then spent about 45 minutes introducing five new Echo smart speakers and displays — the Echo Show 16, Echo Time, Alexa Photo Frame, Echo Studio with Home Camera, and a new Echo Dot — with each product sitting on plinths in the warehouse-like space.

articles.title: DeepMind unveils Genie 4 world model promising more realistic physics and humans
articles.summary:
Last year, Google DeepMind sent gaming stocks tumbling with the reveal of its Genie 3 world model. Since then, world models have become a major focus of AI labs around the world, but Google isn’t resting on its laurels. Researchers have been hard at work on an updated model that improves on Genie 3 in almost every way. And if you pay Google enough money, you might actually get to use Genie 4 before too long.
It’s easy to look at the output of Genie 4 and see a video game, which is why Genie 3 caused so much consternation in the gaming industry. DeepMind doesn’t think about it that way, though. According to Google, world models are a key element in the march toward artificial general intelligence (AGI). A world model creates a virtual world, but it doesn’t require pre-rendering environments or programming interactive elements. You simply tell the model what you want, and it generates the experience frame by frame in real time as you explore it.
DeepMind says this technology could create infinite training environments for physical robots or unlock new avenues of rapid prototyping for creative fields. Of course, that requires the model to accurately simulate what you want. Genie 4 has several improvements that make its simulations more useful, and that’s thanks in part to Google’s updated Gemini models.
When you prompt a world into existence in Genie 4, it leverages Gemini 3.8 Flash as a guiding agent to break down goals and evaluate each output frame. This helps keep the simula…

articles.title: Bank of America kindly asks that you don't share your banking password with your AI assistant | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Financial giant Bank of America is reminding customers to bank safely by kindly not sharing your banking credentials with your AI agent.
In an email blast to customers titled “Protecting your finances in the Al World,” Bank of America urged customers to never share their username and password with another person or an outside service, “including an Al-enabled tool or agent that offers to act on your behalf.”
You can practically sense the frustration in the person sending the email. Still, customers are increasingly handing over their log-ins as personal AI assistants grow more popular. Sharing your banking username and password with an AI assistant runs the risk that it could do something with your finances without your knowledge, or that your bank thinks someone’s raiding your account and locks you out of it. Worse, a security flaw in the AI assistant could result in it leaking your banking credentials elsewhere, giving financially motivated hackers a way into your bank account.
This latest warning comes as banks are still exploring how AI agents fit into the financial world but are reportedly grappling with unauthorized agents accessing their customers’ money. As we discussed onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt, banks, payment providers, and processors are still trying to figure out how to allow customers access to their bank accounts using AI tools, such as for agentic payments, which allow people to set agents to autonomously buy things at the best price or the right time.

- Source:
- Norwegian University of Science and Technology
- Summary:

The breakthrough could help make brain-like computers a reality, potentially enabling dramatically smaller and more energy-efficient technology.

Although most people have never heard of skyrmions, these microscopic magnetic vortices may eventually play an important role in how computers store and process data.
A study published in the journal Nature Nanotechnology provides new insights into how skyrmions behave and how scientists can control them. The findings could help researchers develop smaller, more efficient computing systems and advance emerging quantum technologies.

articles.title: Chuva avança pelo Brasil e traz risco de temporais em cinco regiões
articles.summary:
Áreas de diferentes regiões do Brasil devem receber chuva nesta quarta-feira (28) e quinta-feira (29). A instabilidade também avança sobre o Sudeste e o Sul, com risco de temporais em algumas localidades.
No MATOPIBA, região que abrange partes do Maranhão, Tocantins, Piauí e Bahia, a previsão é de chuva. Já no extremo Norte e em áreas do Nordeste, o calor continua forte, com temperaturas próximas de 40 °C.
Temporais atingem áreas agrícolas
No Norte, as precipitações se concentram principalmente no Acre, Amazonas, Rondônia, Pará e Tocantins. O Centro-Oeste também terá chuva em praticamente toda a região na quarta-feira, com intensificação prevista para partes de Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul e Goiás no dia seguinte.
No Sudeste, a instabilidade ganha força em áreas de São Paulo e Minas Gerais, com possibilidade de chuva também no Rio de Janeiro e no Espírito Santo. Na quinta-feira, as precipitações voltam a avançar pelo Sul, sobretudo no Paraná. O Recôncavo Baiano também está sob atenção devido à previsão de chuvas expressivas.
A mudança no tempo está relacionada ao afastamento de uma área de alta pressão em direção ao oceano Atlântico. Com esse movimento, o ar quente e úmido avança sobre o centro-sul do país, favorecendo a formação de áreas de instabilidade.
Entre os principais destaques da previsão estão:
- MATOPIBA: chuva em áreas agrícolas do Maranhão, Tocantins, Piauí e Bahia, com possibilidade de trovoadas.
- Norte: tempo seco e temperaturas elevadas em áreas de Roraima…

articles.title: Carreteras estrechas y más tráfico: GTA 6 buscará hacer más realista la conducción dentro del juego
articles.summary:
GTA 6 tendrá carreteras más estrechas y tráfico más denso que GTA 5, dos decisiones de diseño con las que Rockstar busca que conducir por sus ciudades resulte más realista y exigente. La información procede de Jason Schreier, periodista de Bloomberg, quien la compartió tras hablar con Aaron Garbut, director artístico y codirector de Rockstar North. No se trata de una confirmación sobre todos los detalles del sistema de conducción, sino de una característica del diseño del mundo descrita por el directivo.
La diferencia puede modificar la manera de recorrer Vice City. En GTA 5, muchas vías anchas permiten acelerar, cambiar de carril y adelantar con relativa facilidad. En la nueva entrega, los espacios más reducidos y la presencia de más vehículos podrían obligar a los jugadores a calcular mejor sus maniobras, frenar con más frecuencia y buscar el momento adecuado para adelantar.
Rockstar no ha explicado todavía con detalle cómo responderán los vehículos ni qué reglas seguirá la inteligencia artificial del tráfico. Por eso, el efecto final sobre la conducción dependerá también de la física de los coches, el comportamiento de los personajes controlados por el juego y la forma en que se gestionen los atascos y las colisiones.

Les propriétaires ont désormais accès à une plateforme pour savoir si un candidat à la location cumule au moins 3 mois de loyers impayés. Un fichier pour consulter et inscrire les locataires

La Guardia Civil ha detenido a una mujer de 29 años en Cangas do Morrazo (Pontevedra) por su presunta participación en múltiples sucesos de hurto y una estafa continuada, con un perjuicio económico superior a los 47.280 euros, según las investigaciones. articles.title: TLS Flaws Found in GoAhead Web Server Used in Hundreds of Millions of Devices
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity firm FoxIO has disclosed three vulnerabilities in GoAhead’s handling of TLS. They could keep revoked client certificates working, let eavesdroppers decrypt some traffic, or help attackers get around a cap on certificate chain length.
GoAhead, a lightweight web server made by EmbedThis, runs the management interfaces of networking equipment, printers and industrial systems. According to FoxIO, it is present on hundreds of millions of devices across the IoT, OT, firewall and military sectors.
FoxIO’s Sébastien Féry, who documented the flaws this week, said each one affects only a subset of deployments. Which GoAhead devices are at risk depends on the TLS library the manufacturer built into the firmware and how it configured certificate checks.
The critical flaw, CVE-2026-115881 (CVSS score of 9.1), impacts GoAhead 3.4.5 through 6.1.0 when built with OpenSSL or a compatible library and configured for mutual TLS (mTLS) with a certificate revocation list (CRL). The server reads the list but never tells OpenSSL to consult it.
On these builds, a certificate an administrator has revoked, such as one tied to a stolen or compromised device, is still accepted, even with issuer verification switched on. Nothing at startup warns that revocation checks are inactive.
The eavesdropping risk comes from the second bug (CVSS score of 5.9, no CVE), found in GoAhead 4.0.2 through 6.1.0 builds that use Mbed TLS. A coding error weakens the encryption of some TLS 1.2 connections enough…

articles.title: AWS Shows Use of AI Agents to Triage Linux Kernel CVEs
articles.summary:
Engineers from Amazon Web Services (AWS) have described how the team that maintains the Linux kernel for EC2 infrastructure handles kernel CVEs. The process combines an automated filter, an AI agent and human review. The team also argues that it needs to move to newer long-term-support (LTS) kernels, as older branches collect fixes that are never backported.
Dylan Johnson and Justinien Bouron gave the talk at the Linux Plumbers Conference in Prague earlier this month. At the start of the recording, Johnson explains that the team maintains the kernel used within EC2 infrastructure. This is separate from Amazon Linux and from the kernels that customers run in their virtual machines.
After the kernel project became a CVE Numbering Authority in February 2024, the team saw about two kernel CVEs a week before 2024 and about 16 a day afterwards, with 848 published on 15 August 2026. The kernel CVE documentation states that the project cannot know how a given system uses the kernel, so users must decide which CVEs apply to them.
The first stage of AWS's process does not use AI. Bouron explained that kernel CVE records are published in JSON and list the affected versions and source files. A script discards a CVE if the kernel version is outside the affected range, or if none of the listed files are built into the image. In AWS's environment this removes about 70% of CVEs, although Bouron said the figure depends heavily on kernel configuration.
The remaining CVEs go to an AI agent. It …

articles.title: Microsoft releases Windows OOB updates to distrust eMudhra certificates
articles.summary:
Microsoft has released out-of-band (OOB) Windows updates to remove trust in certificates tied to compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys, protecting systems that do not receive automatic certificate trust updates.
The KB5134133 update for Windows 11 versions 24H2, 25H2, and 26H2 and the KB5134125 update for Windows 10 versions 21H2 and 22H2 were released on October 26.
The updates are for systems without Internet access, devices that cannot access Microsoft's certificate-update service, and those where automatic Certificate Trust List (CTL) updates have been disabled.
The updates were released after the discovery of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority private keys that were so weak they could be recovered almost instantly.
All eight keys were generated in April 2025 and had values smaller than 256, allowing anyone to recover them by testing just 256 possible numbers.
The compromised keys could have allowed attackers to forge certificates for legitimate websites and intercept encrypted communications.
After the disclosure, eMudhra revoked the eight compromised intermediate certificates, and Mozilla, Google, Apple, and other software vendors also began revoking them.
In response, Microsoft previously updated the Windows Disallowed Certificate Trust List to block the eight affected intermediate certificate authorities, including six used for TLS and two for code signing.

articles.title: Ante la amenaza de la gripe A, España va a optar por vacunar a humanos antes que por seguir sacrificando aves
articles.summary:
La amenaza de la gripe aviar ha dejado de ser un problema que afecta únicamente a los veterinarios, puesto que también ha aparecido en la agenda de la salud pública europea. Y España está muy interesada en ello, puesto que los últimos datos del Centro Europeo para la Prevención y el Control de Enfermedades (ECDC) apuntan a que nuestro país es una de las tres regiones europeas, junto a Noruega y Croacia, para iniciar una campaña de vacunación en humanos contra el virus de la gripe A.
Lo que sabemos. El informe del ECDC publicado a principios de este mismo mes expone el mapa actual de la vacunación zoonótica en Europa, y tras encuestar a 30 países de la UE, el panorama es desigual, ya que ocho países ya tienen recomendaciones nacionales, ocho las están desarrollando y once carecen de planes. Y aquí España entra en el grupo de los que lanzarán su campaña a corto plazo, pero con matices.
Y es que, mientras que en el resto de países europeos las recomendaciones de vacunación se aplican a todas las personas de los grupos de riesgo como ganaderos, trabajadores de mataderos o veterinarios, España ha restringido el cerco. articles.title: Un tournant historique pour l'IA : Anthropic s'apprête à entrer en Bourse avec une croissance monstrueuse
articles.summary:
Anthropic, l’entreprise derrière Claude, s’apprête à entrer à la Bourse de Wall Street pour vendre une partie de ses actions. Et avec le succès de l’intelligence artificielle générative, il se pourrait bien que ce soit un succès. Succès a priori paradoxal puisque la société perd des dizaines de milliards de dollars à chaque semestre. À l’approche de cette entrée en Bourse, Anthropic a partagé son dossier d’introduction qui permet d’en apprendre plus sur sa santé financière.
Une croissance hors norme, mais avec de lourdes pertes
Au premier trimestre de cette année, Anthropic a enregistré un chiffre d’affaires de 16,286 milliards de dollars, contre 1,1 milliard un an plus tôt. Ce qui représente une croissance annuelle d’environ… 1 300%. Et sur l’ensemble de l’année 2025, ses revenus avaient atteint près de 4,6 milliards de dollars, après avoir été multipliés par 12.
Si cette croissance est impressionnante, elle ne se fait pas à n’importe quel prix. La perte nette du premier semestre 2026 est évaluée à 80,75 milliards de dollars, contre 13 milliards un an plus tôt. L’essentiel, soit environ 72 milliards de dollars, provient de charges comptables liées à la variation de la valeur d’obligations convertibles en actions, qui avaient été émises lors de précédentes levées de fonds. Autrement dit, lorsque la valorisation d’Anthropic augmente, la valeur de ces obligations augmente aussi. Healthy snack brand Troovy raises Rs 100 Cr in Series B round led by Fireside Ventures
Gurugram-based Troovy will use the funding for R&D, expanding its manufacturing capacity, and scaling distribution across quick commerce and offline channels.
Troovy, a food and snacks brand, has raised Rs 100 crore in a Series B round of funding led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Sharrp Ventures and other investors.
The Gurugram-based brand will use the funding for R&D, expanding its manufacturing capacity, and scaling distribution across quick commerce and offline channels, as it looks to launch a wide range of products.
Troovy was founded in 2023 by Mansi Baranwal and Aditya Mukherjee with the goal of providing nutritious food. Its portfolio spans categories such as snacks, sauces and spreads, and millet pasta. It says its vacuum-cooked potato chips have 10-12% oil and high protein, compared with 35-40% oil in mainstream chips. It also promises clean-label ketchups and seasonings without synthetic additives or preservatives.
Troovy's co-founder & CBO Aditya Mukherjee said, "This backing (investment) is a vote of confidence in a model most food companies don't use: building with the people who'll actually eat what you make. articles.title: Poland’s Autofixer raises €3 million in venture debt to scale its online car parts platform | EU-Startups
articles.summary:
Autofixer, a Polish online car parts platform, has raised €3 million in venture debt financing to expand further across Europe, develop its platform and grow its team.
The financing came from Orbit Capital, a growth-stage venture debt and growth equity firm, whose portfolio includes Preply, Booksy, MEWS, Rohlik, among others. The venture debt financing allows Autofixer to access capital without diluting existing shareholders.
“The company’s rapid growth and strong business metrics demonstrate both clear product-market fit and the effectiveness of its business model. At this stage, venture debt is a natural way to support further growth, providing additional capital to scale the business without diluting existing shareholders,” said Wiktor Namysł, General Partner at Orbit Capital.
Autofixer was founded in 2021 by the team behind Renee and born2be, two e-commerce brands that were later consolidated under AZA Group. The group generated approximately €114 million in annual revenue at its peak, and the founders are bringing that expertise to the automotive parts market. The earlier growth was backed by Montis Capital, which invested in the company in both 2023 and 2025.
The premise is simple: buying car parts online is harder than it looks. The 360 million vehicles in Europe require a wide range of components, and even within a single model, parts can differ significantly across production years and trim levels. articles.title: The hidden failure paths that affect Kubernetes control plane availability
articles.summary:
The hidden failure paths that affect Kubernetes control plane availability
Kubernetes control planes are designed to contain individual failures, but their availability still depends on how components in the critical path behave under pressure. At fleet scale, a component does not have to crash to contribute to an outage. A valid mechanism can amplify a local defect through shared metadata, synchronized startup work, or an overly aggressive health check.
For example, an informer gives a controller a local view of cluster state, letting its workers make progress without repeatedly querying the API server. This is efficient when controllers start independently. When many controllers restart simultaneously across a fleet, rebuilding those views can place significant pressure on the control plane. The informer mechanism itself becomes the amplifier.
“At fleet scale, a component does not have to crash to contribute to an outage. A valid mechanism can amplify a local defect through shared metadata, synchronized startup work, or an overly aggressive health check.”
This article examines three cases. In the first, an extension API server published an invalid schema after a dependency upgrade and blocked clients that had never used its API. In the second, DaemonSet agents restarted across a large fleet, turning routine startup work into a request storm the API server couldn’t absorb. articles.title: Ford simplifies using your EV as a home battery with the $30K Fathom
articles.summary:
This morning, Ford revealed that buyers of the forthcoming Fathom—the company’s sub-$30,000 electric pickup truck due next year—will get more than just a truck. Until now, vehicle-to-home technology—like the setup Ford developed for the now-discontinued F-150 Lightning—takes DC power from the electric vehicle and runs it through an inverter built into the wallbox to turn it into AC the house can use. But with the Fathom, that inverter is built into the truck from the start. So every Fathom will be able to act as a backup battery for your home.
It’s typical: You wait a decade for a cheap electric truck, and then two come along almost at once. And they’re two radically different products from two radically different automakers that I think will reveal a few preferences from the EV-buying public. One is the Blank Slate, from a brand new startup offering a bare-bones two-door that capitalizes on features the Internet says it wants, like no onboard modem, no touchscreens, and no infotainment system.
The other is the result of one of Detroit’s big three taking a long, hard look at Chinese EVs and asking itself, “How do we make a car that cheap?” Although the Ford Fathom will cost $5,000 more than a Slate, that money does buy an extra pair of doors, modern conveniences like an infotainment system, CarPlay, electric windows, and a vast dealership network to service the car. That may be helpful given how many recalls Ford issues each year.

“La vida es corta para andar con gente sin recursos” resume una de las ideas asociadas a Jeff Bezos sobre la formación de equipos de trabajo. El fundador de Amazon convirtió una librería online creada en 1994 en una compañía con presencia en comercio electrónico, logística, entretenimiento y computación en la nube.
Detrás de ese recorrido hubo decisiones empresariales arriesgadas, pero también una visión sobre las personas que deben participar en un proyecto.
La frase no se refiere necesariamente al dinero, los contactos o la formación académica. En este caso, contar con recursos significa tener la capacidad de responder ante un problema, buscar alternativas y avanzar cuando faltan herramientas, información o experiencia previa.
Para los equipos de tecnología y negocios, esa actitud puede marcar la diferencia entre una dificultad que bloquea el trabajo y una oportunidad para corregir el rumbo.
Jeff Bezos y la importancia de las personas resolutivas
El planteamiento atribuido a Jeff Bezos pone el foco en una cualidad concreta: la iniciativa. Una persona resolutiva identifica un obstáculo y trata de encontrar una salida. Puede aprender una habilidad, solicitar ayuda, revisar procesos o proponer una alternativa sin esperar de forma permanente una indicación externa.
Desde esa perspectiva, el valor de un profesional no depende solo de los conocimientos que acumula al comenzar un empleo. También cuenta su reacción ante tareas desconocidas, problemas inesperados y cambios de priori…

articles.title: How technology is driving manufacturing's next leap

Technology has become part of how modern businesses operate. The more difficult question for business leaders is deciding where they can create meaningful value.
Every year brings new tools, platforms and applications that promise to make businesses faster, more efficient and more competitive. Keeping up with all of them is neither practical nor necessary. What matters is understanding the problems within the business that technology can genuinely help solve and having a clear way to measure whether it has made a difference.
That means technology decisions belong directly in executive and strategic discussions. They dictate how work gets done, how choices are framed, how capital and human resources are deployed, and how rapidly an organisation can pivot. While technical teams lead implementation, deployment decisions must remain tightly aligned with overall business priorities.
The most pragmatic starting point is operational diagnosis: Where is time being lost? Where are decisions constrained by limited data? Which processes introduce unnecessary friction or cost? Addressing these concrete pain points provides a far stronger foundation than selecting a technology and searching for a problem to solve.

articles.title: Intel "Crescent Island" GPU Die Shows Up: 32 Xe3P Cores and 256 XMX Engines
articles.summary:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
Intel "Crescent Island" GPU Die Shows Up: 32 Xe3P Cores and 256 XMX Engines
Intel recently announced its D-series "Crescent Island" inference graphics cards, based on the Xe3P GPU microarchitecture, with the D270 being the highest-end SKU. The company's website has added a GPU bare die shot, revealing that the card is not the massive chip one might expect, but rather something seemingly smaller. The D270 GPU SKU features 32 Xe3P cores, 256 XMX engines, and 32 MB of unified L2 cache. The XMX engines have been redesigned from the four-deep systolic design of the regular Xe3 to 16-deep processing on the Xe3P. This card is intended for AI inferencing rather than training, so silicon requirements are secondary, and the card is rated for up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X.
Additional details include support for the FP4 data format alongside FP8, as well as large register files of 1 MB per core and an L1 cache of 512 KB per core. In total, there are 256 Vector engines and 256 of the new XMX engines, each divided into groups of eight per Xe3P core. Furthermore, the Xe3P lacks graphics processing elements for outputting imagery, as the silicon is designed purely for AI inference workloads that require long context and agentic tasks. articles.title: How Anthropic Redesigned Source Control for AI-Driven Development
articles.summary:
Anthropic recently detailed how it migrated its monorepo from Git to Scion. Scion is a source control system that moves repository operations to the server side and uses content-addressed storage and tiered caches for agent and CI workloads. The design sacrifices offline independence for less local data and shared infrastructure.
In its 13 October engineering post, Anthropic reported that daily merged changes rose from around 2,500 in May to more than 30,000 in September. Its CI systems perform approximately 25 million checkouts daily, against a monorepo with nearly 100 GB of main-branch history and a compressed working copy exceeding 25 GB. The company had used shallow clones, sparse checkouts, promisor remotes, repository snapshots and several hundred Git mirrors, but said these became harder to operate as merge rates increased.
Daily merged changes in Anthropic’s monorepo from January to September 2026. (Source)
Scion puts commits, merges, rebases, history and blame queries on the server. Clients maintain bounded object caches and virtualised checkouts materialise files on demand. Tools can query diffs and perform some writes through APIs without checking out code.
A Scion changeset records the files that have changed relative to its first parent, with content-addressed pointers to the compressed file contents in blob storage. Creating changesets is separate from updating references, so accepting changesets requires no cross-server coordination. For history and blame queri…

Bislang galt das äußere Sonnensystem in der Wissenschaft als ein äußerst stabiles Konstrukt, bei dem selbst nach dem Tod der Sonne in einigen Milliarden Jahren die äußeren Planeten für weitere 30 bis 100 Milliarden Jahre geordnet auf ihren Bahnen verbleiben sollten. Zwar wird unsere Sonne als Roter Riese vermutlich die inneren Planeten zerstören, doch erst externe galaktische Einflüsse galten als endgültige Bedrohung für Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus und Neptun.

Stormbreaker Ventures led the round, bringing the company’s total funding to $9 million.
When the company first approached this problem, it looked at sports. When a basketball hits the court, fans are stomping in the stands and bass pounds through the arena’s speakers – all of this comes through microphones at the same time. For an artificial intelligence system trying to isolate the dribble, those overlapping sounds can make this difficult.
This challenge sits at the center of Edge Sound Research’s approach to machine perception: connecting audio with tracking and visual data to determine which sound belongs to which object.
“The issue in audio is it’s not object oriented; it’s channel oriented,” co-founder and Chief Executive Valtteri Salomaki told SiliconANGLE in an interview.
For broadcasters, making that connection means following a player’s sounds through a crowded arena. Edge is betting the same approach could help robots and other physical AI systems interpret the world around them — including activity their cameras cannot yet see.

articles.title: Nebius cut rollout collection time by 66.9% — here’s what changed
articles.summary:
Nebius cut rollout collection time by 66.9% — here’s what changed
In AI agent training, you can pay for powerful GPUs and still spend much of your time waiting. Agents need to attempt tasks and produce results before the model can learn from them. A few slow attempts can hold up the next training update, making the systems that run those tasks a major factor in training speed and cost.
Di Jin, VP of AI Training at Amsterdam-headquartered Nebius, says teams coming from pretraining or supervised fine-tuning can underestimate the work these systems do.
“If you staff and design it as a training project, inference becomes the bottleneck nobody owns.”
Rollout generation often takes most of a training step’s wall-clock time, making batching, cache management and scheduling central to how fast the model can learn. “If you staff and design it as a training project, inference becomes the bottleneck nobody owns,” Jin says.
Time to a trainable batch
He adds that engineers should measure time to a trainable batch alongside throughput. Average tokens per second can hide the long tail: in a synchronous batch, the step cannot finish until the final trajectory is completed.
Agent trajectories do not all have the same length. Many finish quickly, while others take longer, leaving training GPUs waiting on a handful of stragglers. For this reason, Jin advises engineers to treat the inference engine as part of the post-training reinforcement learning optimizer.

articles.title: Uber Moves beyond CPU Cores with Performance-Aware Scheduling for Stateful Workloads
articles.summary:
Uber has introduced Normalized Compute Units (NCUs) to make CPU allocation more consistent across its highly heterogeneous server fleet. The approach, implemented in Uber's Odin stateful orchestration platform, accounts for differences in processor performance rather than treating every CPU core as equivalent.
Odin manages around 5 million CPU cores across on-premises data centres and public clouds, including multiple generations of x86 hardware and ARM processors. Uber found that single-threaded performance can vary by almost a factor of two between the fastest and slowest cores. Consequently, the same workload can require significantly different numbers of physical CPU cores depending on where it runs.
The problem creates two competing risks. Allocating resources according to the slowest hardware can waste capacity on faster machines, while allocating according to average usage can leave workloads under-provisioned when they move to slower servers. For stateful workloads, where moving traffic to another machine is often not possible, the latter can become a reliability problem.
Uber's solution is to separate the amount of compute performance a workload requires from the physical cores used to provide it.
Odin assigns each server type a performance factor, using an older server generation as a baseline of 100. Newer hardware can have considerably higher values; Uber reports factors approaching 190 for some servers. These factors are initially determined during hardware quali…

articles.summary:
2026 est une année noire pour les fabricants de portefeuilles crypto (hardware wallets). Ces boîtiers de petite taille servent à stocker hors ligne des bitcoins, et d’autres cryptomonnaies, afin de les protéger contre d’éventuelles tentatives de piratage. Malheureusement, ce sont désormais les concepteurs de portefeuilles qui se retrouvent dans le colimateur des cybercriminels.
Récemment, la licorne française Ledger a subi une attaque dite « de la chaîne d’approvisionnement ». Those are key, of course, but by themselves they fail to tell you what amount of useful compute power your system brings. In the end, we’re pushing our technology to get it to a useful scale, which in the most basic sense means that value per solution must outweigh cost per solution.
Quantum computers hold real promise in utility applications, be it in faster drug discovery, accelerating materials research, or enabling more efficient machine learning once they run at a useful scale. Getting there means taking the cost of running these machines as seriously as the physics behind them to make them economical. A better understanding of how much useful compute power systems generate for each unit of energy or dollar you put into it is key for that.

articles.title: Modders unlock hidden AI power on Nvidia RTX 20, 30, and 40 series GPUs, nearly doubling some benchmarks
articles.summary:
Sounding off: A used RTX 3090 has become the go-to card for running AI models at home, mostly because 24GB of memory costs far less on a gaming card than on a workstation one. That bargain comes with a catch Nvidia prints in its own spec sheets, though. On GeForce cards, one of the most common kinds of AI math runs at exactly half speed. A few open-source projects now claim to remove that limitation on RTX 20-, 30-, and 40-series cards.
The limit lives in the tensor cores. When they multiply FP16 or BF16 numbers and add up the results in higher-precision FP32, GeForce cards issue those instructions at half the rate of the FP16-accumulate mode. That FP32 mode is the one most training and plenty of inference actually rely on. The workstation cards Nvidia builds on the same chips – the RTX A6000, for example – run it at full speed.
The first fix came from GitHub user Zagitta, who published "gpu-unlock" for RTX 30-series cards. It's a Linux kernel module that kicks in before Nvidia's driver loads. That's when it rewrites two speed-select registers on the GPU and resets the card. Nvidia's regular driver then takes over as usual, so nobody has to flash a VBIOS or patch a driver.
On an RTX 3090 Ti capped at 450W, the developer's matrix-multiply tests show BF16 throughput climbing from 87.5 to 157.4 TFLOPS. TF32 nearly doubled, too. FP16 saw a smaller gain of 35%.

Die geografischen Pole der Erde verschieben sich derzeit mit einer per Satellit gemessenen Geschwindigkeit von rund zehn Zentimetern pro Jahr, was die durchschnittliche Driftgeschwindigkeit tektonischer Platten übersteigt.
