articles.title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
articles.summary:
Defenders across the world face the burden of responding to yet another botched code-execution vulnerability, this time in boot-time firmware used by most of the world’s server vendors and data centers.
The vulnerability, with a severity rating of 9.5 out of 10, resides in the TianoCore EDK II, an open source codebase that hardware makers and cloud providers use to create the UEFI firmware that runs during the boot-up sequence. Last year, a representative of the UEFI Forum called EDK2 the “preeminent solution / implementation of the UEFI specifications.” Virtually all UEFI suppliers (sometimes still called IBVs or independent BIOS vendors), including AMI, Insyde, and Phoenix, use the reference code extensively. Project Mu, Microsoft’s hardened EDK2 fork, used the code containing the vulnerable component as well.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, is a memory-corruption flaw in an ICMP component that attackers can exploit to execute malicious code that runs before the operating system and firmware can implement defenses like Secure Boot, which establishes a chain of trust for all code, including the Trusted Platform Module (TPM), loaded during boot. While final payloads delivered by CVE-2026-97631 have no persistence—meaning they run only once—they can give attackers a wide opening to install other payloads that also run each time early in the boot process.
The cat has left the bag

articles.title: Building an Offline-First AI Coding Tutor for Low-End Android Phones
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- On low-end devices in low-bandwidth markets, a full storage volume is a normal operating condition rather than an edge case, so any await on a cache or database write inside a critical render path is a latent blank screen and should be treated as a non-fatal degradation instead.
- localStorage is the wrong persistence layer for any cache that scales with content or locale, because its roughly 5MB ceiling and synchronous API impose the heaviest cost on precisely the underpowered devices you are trying to serve, while IndexedDB with a dual-read migration window lets you move without stranding existing users.
- WebAssembly runtimes such as Pyodide and sql.js make server-free code execution viable on smartphones, but only if you defer initialisation into a Web Worker and treat cold-start cost as a first-class UX problem rather than a benchmark footnote.
- AI features that depend on a hosted endpoint should be designed with an explicit degradation contract, which includes a defined second tier, a defined timeout, persisted session state across the switch, and feedback formats that stay useful when the weaker model answers.
- Discoverability and usability are different properties, and a feature placed outside a user's working line of sight is functionally a feature that does not exist.

articles.title: AI agents need to be replaceable – without losing your work
articles.summary:
AI agents need to be replaceable – without losing your work
An agent receives approval to process a partial refund. It sends the request to a payment API, and the process crashes. Maybe the payment service completed the refund. Maybe the request never went through. A replacement agent spins up and finds an operation record marked dispatched with no outcome written.
This kind of ambiguity isn’t unique to agents. Any distributed worker crashing mid-mutation faces the same problem. But a conventional worker resumes a predetermined workflow from the last checkpoint. An agent does something more dangerous: it reasons on its own. Given the same customer request and no outcome record, it might come up with a different plan, pick different parameters, or decide to issue a new refund instead of continuing the one already approved.
“An agent does something more dangerous: it reasons on its own.”
If the original refund went through, a second attempt refunds the customer twice. The charge still has enough remaining balance to cover another partial refund, so nothing stops it.
The replacement must inherit the original operation, not reinterpret it.
The operation must outlive the agent
An agent’s process, its in-memory variables, its transient reasoning context: all disposable. The business operation is not. The refund, its approval, its parameters, its current status. articles.summary:
On Tuesday, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) confirmed that hackers have begun exploiting a critical Brotli vulnerability known as Node2Shell, Broccoli2Shell, and HTTP2Shell.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111497, this critical-severity flaw stems from an out-of-bounds write weakness in the Brotli decoder used to expand data compressed with Google's widely popular Brotli lossless compression algorithm.
Unprivileged attackers can use a maliciously crafted Brotli-compressed stream to trigger crashes or memory leaks and, in some cases, gain remote code execution on devices with vulnerable Brotli libraries or binaries.
The security issue was first identified in the Node.js JavaScript runtime environment, but it also affects HTTP servers and clients that rely on vulnerable Brotli implementations.
On Sunday, Microsoft also pushed an emergency .NET security update, warning that attackers could exploit it to escalate privileges on systems with a vulnerable .NET version.
CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday and ordered US government agencies to patch their systems within two weeks, by November 10, as mandated by its Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.

articles.title: Chrome Opens Trial for the Email Verification API: Letting Sites Verify Without Sending Emails
articles.summary:
Google has opened a Chrome origin trial for the Email Verification API, a WICG proposal that lets a browser confirm a visitor owns the email address they typed, without sending a single message. The trial began in Chrome 150 on desktop, with Gmail taking part as the first participating provider.
The idea replaces the familiar one-time code or magic link. Today a user enters an email, leaves for their inbox, copies a code, and returns, a context switch that often loses them. The proposal uses a three-party model where the browser sits between the site (the "verifier") and the mailbox provider (the "issuer"). If the user is already signed in to their provider, the browser quietly fetches a signed token and drops it into the form, and the server validates that token on submission. Google notes the issuer never learns which site made the request.
For developers the front end implementation is fairly straightforward. The email field needs an autocomplete hint, plus a hidden input carrying a session-bound nonce:
<input id="email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email">
<input type="hidden" name="token" nonce={nonce} autocomplete="email-verification-token">
The heavier work sits on the server side, where the token's signature is checked against the provider's keys. Resend's Phil Nash, who wrote a walkthrough of the flow, published an npm package and a Next.js example to handle that parsing and validation.

The federal government is considering adding gaming platforms to its digital safety bill to stop predators from using those platforms to target kids.
There are a number of gaming platforms that allow adults to communicate with children, which has sparked concerns over predatory behaviours like grooming.
Roblox has become one of the chief platforms of concern, with about 40 per cent of the game’s over 85 million players being under the age of 13. articles.title: China's top-secret spaceplane can't hide in low-Earth orbit
articles.summary:
A winged Chinese spacecraft bearing a strong resemblance to the US military’s X-37B spaceplane was photographed in orbit by a passing US-owned commercial satellite in 2024, and we finally have the image.
The Chinese spaceplane has delta wings, payload bay doors, a dark heat shield, and a rear-mounted service module with power-generating solar arrays. In other words, the design of the winged ship is, to a great degree, a copy of the X-37B spaceplane flown by the US Space Force.
The photo was taken by a commercial imaging satellite owned by a company called Vantor, known as Maxar in 2024. Vantor is one of several companies that provide reconnaissance imagery of locations around the world to the US military and US intelligence agencies. The same Earth-imaging satellites can point their telescopes at objects in space.
Lower-resolution views of a Chinese spaceplane showing the vehicle’s general shape were publicly available before the DIA assessment. articles.title: Post-quantum cryptography: Dell secures the root of trust - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Dell brings post-quantum cryptography to the root of trust
Post-quantum cryptography is gaining urgency as attackers collect encrypted data they hope to decrypt later with quantum computers.
Stolen data is only part of the problem. A future quantum computer could also forge the signatures that tell a laptop or server its firmware is genuine, according to Rick Martinez (pictured, right), fellow and vice president of client solutions at Dell Technologies Inc. Code written by an attacker would then pass the same checks as code from the manufacturer.
“We think of this in terms of trust now, forge later,” Martinez said. “Instead of kind of attacking that confidentiality of encryption of data, these quantum computers will actually be able to attack the integrity of the actual system that runs everything from the bottom up.”
Martinez and Judy Furlong (center), senior distinguished engineer at Dell, spoke with theCUBE’s Krista Case (left) at the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how enterprises can protect firmware and storage as they transition to post-quantum cryptography. (* Disclosure below.)

El gobernador Hoedaack soltaba una risa aguda en unos aposentos de color blanco nuclear y palmeaba la espalda de este Darth Vader primigenio, un general alto y de gesto sombrío que apenas esbozaba una sonrisa. Era un general imperial sin más y la escena está en el borrador de 'The Star Wars' que Lucas terminó ese mes. Ahí, su nombre aparece mencionado por primera vez.

articles.title: South Carolina's measles outbreak jumped to Washington state 5 times in 2 weeks
articles.summary:
Since measles was declared eliminated in the US in 2000, the country’s occasional cases have come mainly from international travelers—visitors from far-flung places where the virus still spreads freely—or unvaccinated US residents who return from abroad with a highly infectious souvenir. But as vaccination rates have slipped nationwide in recent years and outbreaks grow bigger and more frequent, domestic travel now poses a greater risk than international incursions.
In a study published this week in NEJM Evidence, Washington state health officials highlight that risk, detailing how an explosive outbreak in South Carolina reached their distant state through five distinct importation events over two weeks in January. In all, the introductions led to 26 cases among residents before officials stamped out the spread.
South Carolina’s measles outbreak began on October 2, 2025, and was declared over on April 26, 2026. Officials confirmed 997 cases in the state during the outbreak. At the time, it was the largest measles outbreak recorded since the virus was declared eliminated, but Pennsylvania’s ongoing outbreak has since surpassed it.
The study in Washington relied heavily on epidemiological data, linking cases among contacts and exposure sites. articles.title: Airbnb Cuts Recommendation Staleness from 2 Days to Seconds with Chronon
articles.summary:
Airbnb has extended its open source Chronon feature platform with Push Mode and Near Real Time (NRT) Model Transform to update sequence based recommendation embeddings within seconds of guest activity. The change reduced embedding staleness from nearly two days to less than a minute, with typical updates arriving within 10 to 30 seconds. Airbnb also reported a 1.67% improvement in offline NDCG and an approximately 0.33% increase in uncancelled bookings in online A/B testing.
The work builds on Airbnb’s JourneyFormer based sequence recommender, which uses a Transformer encoder to represent a guest’s booking, review and browsing history. Previously, the encoder ran as a daily batch job, generating embeddings that were stored in a low latency store. During a search, the ranking system retrieved the latest embedding and combined it with the live query, keeping the Transformer outside the latency sensitive serving path. However, activity occurring after the daily batch could remain absent from the embedding until the following run, with processing delays bringing effective staleness close to two days.
Airbnb’s initial architecture showing the daily batch sequence encoder, embedding store and online ranking path. (Source : Airbnb Blog Post)

articles.summary:
Durante décadas, un millonario británico dedicó buena parte de su fortuna a contratar trabajadores para excavar un gigantesco laberinto bajo las calles de Liverpool. Nadie sabía qué pretendía conseguir. Los túneles no conducían a ningún lugar concreto, algunos alcanzaban profundidades sorprendentes y su propietario jamás dejó planos ni explicaciones. Tras su muerte, la construcción quedó enterrada bajo toneladas de escombros y el misterio sobrevivió durante casi dos siglos. Ahora, después de 30 años de investigaciones, alguien ha encontrado una respuesta mucho más humana de lo que nadie imaginaba.
El millonario que decidió agujerear Liverpool. Joseph Williamson nació en Yorkshire en 1769 y llegó a Liverpool con apenas 11 años para trabajar en el negocio tabaquero de Richard Tate, cuya hija Elizabeth acabaría convirtiéndose en su esposa. En 1803 asumió el control de la empresa y acumuló una considerable fortuna gracias al comercio y otras inversiones. Tres años después compró terrenos en Edge Hill, entonces una zona poco urbanizada situada a varios kilómetros del centro de Liverpool, con la intención inicial de construir viviendas.
Lo extraordinario llegó después: durante 34 años, hasta su muerte en 1840, mantuvo a numerosos hombres excavando la roca arenisca del subsuelo y levantando túneles, cámaras y estructuras abovedadas. El proyecto fue creciendo hasta convertirse en una construcción cuya verdadera finalidad Williamson nunca explicó públicamente.

Les pirates ont glissé un code malveillant dans ce programme, et récupéraient à chaque commande les informations de carte saisies dans le formulaire, avec le CPF du client. Les banques brésiliennes identifient leurs clients grâce à ce numéro fiscal. L'entreprise néerlandaise de sécurité Sansec a repéré le code malveillant le 24 octobre, et Convertr ne l'a retiré qu'hier. The M6 is split into two variants for the iMac. Picking the “M6 chip with two Thunderbolt ports” option gets you a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, whereas picking “M6 chip with four Thunderbolt ports” gets you 12 cores for each, instead. The two-port variant maxes out at 24 GB of RAM and 1TB of storage, whereas the four-port one maxes out at 32GB of RAM and 2TB of storage.
There’s only one M6 chip option for the MacBook Pro—the one with the 12-core GPU and CPU. It caps out at 32GB of RAM but can go to 4TB of storage.
It’s a more substantial refresh for the iMac, as its previous update introduced the M4. Apple skipped the M5 and went straight to the M6 here. In terms of performance gains moving from the M4 to the M6, Apple said with the Mac mini that users can expect up to 40 percent faster CPU performance, up to double graphics performance, and nearly five times faster on-device AI. articles.title: Researchers set a real-time fiber record: 3.2 petabits per second over 10.3 kilometers
articles.summary:
So Much Internet P0rn: Demand for data processing is surging, and traditional communication standards are no longer up to the job. Thanks to a novel engineering approach, a Chinese team is developing fiber-optic technology that might solve the data speed problem for a while, and then some.
A joint initiative by Chinese researchers and engineers has set a new record for real-time fiber-optic communications. The team sent 3.2 petabits per second (Pbps) through a single optical fiber, topping the 2.5 Pbps mark the same group set earlier this year. The figure reflects bidirectional transmission, with traffic flowing in both directions at once.
One petabit equals 1,000 terabits, which means a 3.2 Pbps connection could download more than 20,000 4K movies in a single second. The researchers said the feat means one fiber-optic cable could, in theory, serve the gigabit broadband needs of 3.2 million households.
The record comes from researchers at CICT's National Key Laboratory of Optical Communication Technologies and Networks, Peng Cheng Laboratory and FiberHome Fujikura. They reached 3.2 Pbps using a 24-core optical fiber over a distance of 10.3 km.
The optical signal was engineered to use thousands of parallel channels across three wavelength bands. The team relied on optical modules it developed in-house, aiming for real-time transfers that could meet current commercial standards.

According to CNBC, Oracle will also add Cerebras Systems Inc.’s wafer-scale accelerators and OpenAI Group PBC’s Jalapeño inference processor. The latter chip is part of a broader partnership that also encompasses several newly revealed cloud services.
Optical network links
Google’s TPUs exchange data using two technologies called ICI and OCS. ICS transmits data via copper wires, while OCS employs optical links. Sending data over an optical link usually requires servers to turn light signals into electricity and then back into light. Google’s OCS technology skips that step, which lowers power usage. It employs tiny mechanical mirrors to steer light beams in the direction of the recipient servers.
The TPUs in Oracle’s data centers will use OCS and ICI technology to exchange data with one another. They will connect to the rest of the host data center using the database giant’s own Acceleron networking technology. Acceleron is powered by a custom SmartNIC, a chip optimized to perform network management and cybersecurity tasks.

Una vez activado el protocolo de emergencia, los trenes se han puesto en marcha.
Ha sido cuando se ha restablecido la circulación cuando el AVE ha alcanzado el tren de Iryo que estaba completamente detenido en la vía porque no había podido retomar la marcha.
El corredor andaluz es la línea de alta velocidad más antigua de nuestro país. Inaugurada en 1992 con la apertura Madrid-Sevilla, utiliza el sistema de seguridad LZB, que también se utiliza en las líneas C-5 de Cercanías en Madrid y toda la red del Euskotren.

articles.title: Steam Frame Gets Mainline Linux Support, Signalling SteamOS Alternatives for VR Gaming
articles.summary:
Tuesday, October 27th 2026
Steam Frame Gets Mainline Linux Support, Signalling SteamOS Alternatives for VR Gaming
The Valve Steam Frame has been supported in downstream SteamOS kernel builds since its launch in September, but a new set of patches submitted for inclusion in the mainline Linux kernel 7.4 will officially add support for the new VR headset in the mainline Linux kernel. The patches were submitted by Neil Armstrong on behalf of Valve Software and provide initial support for the Steam Frame. 
The patch notes specifically mention support for system reserved memory, regulators, GPIO keys PMIC functions, PMIC ADC channels, USB gadget, Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth, I2C and basic peripherals, and the built-in SD card slot. While support isn't yet feature-complete, it lays the groundwork for further kernel support down the line and should make it significantly easier for other distributions to support the Steam Frame without implementing a bunch of custom code and tools. This is also just one of many Linux 7.4 patches that will improve hardware support in the upcoming Linux kernel version.

Un futur article 88 bis du RGPD autoriserait l’entraînement et l’exploitation des IA sur des données personnelles au nom du seul « intérêt légitime », sans que les premiers concernés aient leur mot à dire.
Le droit de dire non passe à la trappe

La Commission avait assorti sa proposition de novembre 2025 d’un garde-fou : un droit d’opposition inconditionnel, qui permettait de retirer ses données d’un entraînement sans se justifier. Le Conseil l’a supprimé. Ne reste que l’opposition classique de l’article 21 du RGPD, qu’une entreprise peut écarter en invoquant des « motifs légitimes et impérieux ». La protection particulière des enfants quitte elle aussi le corps du texte pour un simple considérant.

The report maps any harm to users from Microsoft's PC browser choice practices, focusing on dark patterns that are used by the company.
For those unfamiliar, dark patterns are designs that steer people into choices they wouldn't otherwise make, such as hiding a decline button or making cancellation difficult.
BIT identified 10 dark patterns that it said make it harder to choose a browser other than Edge or subvert a user's choice of an alternative browser after that decision has already been made. These are:

articles.title: Unos científicos desarrollan un dispositivo capaz de unir la luz de varios telescopios y lo probarán en Calar Alto, Almería
articles.summary:
La astronomía ha evolucionado muchísimo en los últimos años. Cada vez se pueden captar objetos más difusos y lejanos, pero todo tiene un límite. Para llegar más lejos, es necesario que los telescopios puedan captar más luz. Eso se consigue con telescopios más grandes, pero, técnicamente hablando, es algo que tiene un límite. Por eso, la ciencia se centra también en la búsqueda de formas de combinar la luz de muchos telescopios pequeños en una sola señal que los instrumentos puedan manipular. Justamente eso es lo que pretende hacer un equipo internacional de científicos, dirigido por el Instituto de Astrofísica de Andalucía (IAA), con su linterna fotónica.
Siete telescopios como si fuesen uno. Las linternas fotónicas son componentes de fibra óptica que sirven para adaptar dos tipos de fibra. Generalmente, se usan para dividir la luz de una sola fibra óptica en varias señales independientes. Sin embargo, estos científicos han logrado hacer justo lo contrario: unir las señales de siete fibras ópticas en una sola. El resultado se puede usar para alimentar cualquier instrumento de los que normalmente emplean la luz captada por los telescopios para obtener información.
En pruebas de laboratorio, se ha logrado conservar más del 90% de la luz original, por lo que sería una herramienta muy útil para observar objetos débiles.

articles.title: Smart TVs spy on you, even when you opt out: study
articles.summary:
A new study has shown that your smart TV might be tracking you and what you watch, even when you opt out of tracking.
The study, named Watching the Watchers, was conducted by researchers affiliated with Northeastern University in Boston, Massachusetts.
- Essentially, it examines automatic content recognition (ACR) features, which the study noted are built into most available smart TVs—and whether turning ACR off actually stops TVs from sending whatever is on your screen to providers.
The researchers tested TVs running Tizen OS (Samsung), Roku OS (Roku, TCL), webOS (LG), SmartCast OS (Vizio), Google TV OS (Sony, Hisense, TCL), Fire TV OS, and others like VIDAA and Xumo.
To add some context, here is how ACR works: essentially, the TV takes short audio or video snapshots of what is on screen, and those snapshots (or the digital fingerprints made from them) are then sent to the internet or ACR provider. From there, the provider compares what was sent to a library of known content to determine exactly what you are watching. The data can reveal your viewing habits and can be used for targeted ads or sold to other companies.
Interestingly, the researchers found out that antenna broadcasts were almost always tracked on every analyzed system. On the streaming side, no TV tracked YouTube or Netflix, but free ad-supported streaming platform Tubi was tracked on Tizen OS, Google TV on Sony, and VIDAA OS.

Los organoides, modelados a partir del prosencéfalo humano, miden menos de un milímetro y contienen alrededor de 10.000 neuronas, además de células de soporte. El experimento, publicado en la revista Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence, buscó determinar si estas redes neuronales podían recibir información táctil y retransmitirla de forma reconocible.

articles.title: Fields Medal-winning UC Berkeley professor ends graded homework due to AI cheating — says in-person exams are the only solution left to widespread AI use
articles.summary:
Fields Medal-winning UC Berkeley professor ends graded homework due to AI cheating — says in-person exams are the only solution left to widespread AI use
AI has gotten so good that it’s increasingly difficult to differentiate between human- and AI-generated homework.
A University of California, Berkeley (UC Berkeley) professor has stopped giving his students graded homework, saying that rampant AI use has made it pointless. According to the New York Post, renowned mathematician Richard Borcherds said that it’s now nearly impossible to tell the difference between a student-written submission and one that’s been created using artificial intelligence. Because of this, he now primarily uses in-person exams with no electronic devices to grade his students and see how well they are doing in his class.
“Online exams are now a waste of time as several students just use AI to answer the questions. I cannot tell which students are using AI, but I notice the average score increases a lot in online exams,” Borcherds told the publication. He also added, “Grading for correctness just adds a huge incentive for them to use AI for homework instead of doing it themselves and penalizes students for honesty. And paying to grade AI generated answers is a waste of time and money.”

Watch out — that Microsoft Teams chat might be hackers impersonating your IT support
Crooks are messaging victims via Teams and offering IT support
- Attackers flood inboxes with spam, then impersonate IT support through Microsoft Teams messages and calls
- Victims are tricked into sharing remote access via Quick Assist, AnyDesk, or ScreenConnect
- Researchers observed 400+ incidents, warning default Teams federation settings enable the social-engineering campaign
Cybersecurity researchers Arctic Wolf have warned of an ongoing, widespread hacking campaign that includes an email inbox flooded with spam messages, a Teams account impersonating IT support, and the use of absolutely legitimate, everyday software.
The goal seems to be persistent access, possibly in preparation of a subsequent malware or ransomware infection.
How the attack plays out
In its report, Arctic Wolf said it observed the same pattern in more than 400 cases. It starts with the victim - an employee in the target company - receiving hundreds, possibly thousands of spam emails in a very short timeframe, so their inbox gets absolutely flooded with junk, burying any and all meaningful, valuable emails under a mountain of trash.
A few moments later, that same person gets a Teams message from a user that, by all accounts, looks legitimate: their name clearly states “IT Service Desk”, and sometimes even has a first name next to it (something along the lines of Liam, Ethan, or Scott). They tell the victim they’ve be…

articles.title: Google Docs agora edita arquivos Markdown nativamente • Tecnoblog
articles.summary:
Google Docs agora edita arquivos Markdown nativamente
Arquivos continuam no formato original e ganham colaboração em tempo real e histórico de versões.
O Google Docs agora aceita arquivos Markdown (.md e .markdown) diretamente, sem que seja preciso transformá-los em documentos no formato próprio do serviço. Com a novidade, é possível trabalhar em um arquivo pelo editor do Google, compartilhá-lo e adicionar comentários mantendo a extensão original.
Markdown é um formato de texto que utiliza caracteres simples para representar elementos como títulos, listas, links e trechos em negrito. Por depender de texto puro, ele é comum em documentação de software, repositórios de código e, mais recentemente, em arquivos utilizados por sistemas de inteligência artificial.
O Google Docs já oferecia algumas ferramentas para trabalhar com Markdown. Desde 2024, era possível importar um arquivo .md, convertê-lo em um documento do Google e depois exportá-lo novamente em Markdown. A diferença agora é que não há conversão.
Ao enviar um arquivo para o Drive e abri-lo no Docs, ele continua armazenado no formato original. O editor passa apenas a mostrar uma versão formatada do conteúdo, como um documento comum, e permite alterá-lo usando a interface tradicional do Docs.
Com o suporte, toda a estrutura de compartilhamento e outras ferramentas da interface do editor de textos pode ser usada nos documentos .md. Os arquivos podem ser editados simultaneamente por diversos usuários sem que seja necessário …

articles.title: Watch this autonomous drone chase a person through a forest without GPS, maps, or cloud computing
articles.summary:
Why it matters: Plenty of off-the-shelf drones can tail a cyclist down a trail these days, but most of them still lean on GPS to keep track of where they are. That's a problem in a forest, where a thick canopy can make the signal pretty unreliable. A lab at Purdue University has now shown off a drone that chases a person through the woods with no GPS at all.
Purdue computer science professor Aniket Bera posted the 44-second video on LinkedIn last Friday. It shows a quadcopter from his IDEAS Lab weaving between trees to keep a person in frame. And the drone works it all out on its own computer, without a map of the forest to rely on. Bera says skipping the cloud matters because a drone banking hard around a thin branch can't afford to wait on a server somewhere.
The person also keeps disappearing behind trunks, of course. For that, Bera's post lists an occlusion prediction step. It has the drone guess where its target is headed until they come back into view.
Navigating without GPS is also exactly the kind of autonomy the US military has been pouring money into. Last November, Purdue announced that the Army Research Laboratory had signed a five-year, $1.5 million deal with Bera's lab to build drones and ground robots that can find their way through hostile terrain without satellites. That said, the LinkedIn post doesn't say whether that money paid for the forest flights.

articles.title: Transitioning Legacy Aircraft Power Architectures to High-Density Switching Supplies - EE Times

Aircraft electrical systems often stay in service for decades, even as avionics demand more from established interfaces. High-density switching supplies offer one way to modernize legacy aircraft power architectures, provided the added power density fits existing integration constraints. For manufacturers weighing an aerospace power supply upgrade, the central question is how much capability a replacement can add without disturbing the platform around it.
The risks of using an outdated aerospace power supply
An outdated aerospace power supply can impose size, weight, and power (SWaP) penalties that crowd out avionics upgrades. The Department of Defense’s commercial microelectronics market share fell from 60% in 1987 to less than 2% in 2024, according to the Defense Logistics Agency. The decline highlights the Defense Department’s diminishing influence in a market increasingly driven by commercial demand. Even so, it may point to procurement exposure for long-lived platforms that depend on parts no longer in production.
Thermal cycling may also degrade aging conversion components, while discontinued semiconductors can complicate repair. Preserving installation interfaces while updating the internal conversion technology gives engineers a targeted path forward. Suppliers such as Behlman provide form-fit-function replacement and modernization options for older or obsolete power supplies. Still, electrical and qualification equivalence need verification before any drop-in swap.

articles.title: "Es un principio básico de respeto": el veto al burka se cuela en las escuelas españolas por la Comunidad Valenciana
articles.summary:
La Comunidad Valenciana ha abierto uno de los melones más espinosos a los que se enfrenta el sistema de educación español: ¿qué hacer con las alumnas (o maestras) que acudan a las aulas con el rostro cubierto por un burka o niqab? Es una cuestión relevante porque, aunque a día de hoy no parece que se den con frecuencia casos así, resulta igualmente innegable que España es cada vez más un país diverso, con una importante población inmigrante y musulmana.
Con ese telón de fondo, en la Comunidad Valenciana lo han tenido claro: los rostros, siempre a la vista.
Rompiendo el melón. Las leyes de acompañamiento de los presupuestos suelen actuar como grandes ‘cajones de sastre’, textos en los que se cuelan medidas que afectan al uso de los recursos públicos y el día a día de las administraciones. La Ley 5/2026 de la Comunidad Valenciana no es una excepción. En su amplio articulado (aprobado el 31 de julio, aunque se publicó hace un mes en el BOE) encontramos medidas relacionadas con tributos, competencias y regulaciones.
Entre esa amalgama hay una medida que, aunque esperada, ha despertado un interés especial: la regulación de ciertas prendas asociadas al mundo islámico en espacios públicos. La ley no habla expresamente de burkas, niqabs o hijabs (de hecho, ni se citan); pero hace algo igual de efectivo: modifica ciertos reglamentos que afectan a los usuarios del transporte público, hospitales y recintos escolares.

Northstar launches with $7M to give AI agents the context to act on security risks
Cybersecurity startup Northstar Security AI Inc. launched today with $7 million in new funding to give artificial intelligence agents the context they need to act on security risks.
Northstar offers a platform that feeds data from a company’s existing security and information technology tools into a real-time Security Context Graph. A known vulnerability, an unmanaged device or an overprivileged account can look manageable on its own.
Put together, the same issues can leave a critical business system exposed. Those toxic combinations are what the graph is meant to find, since the underlying data usually sits in tools that don’t share it.
A company laptop with no endpoint protection is the example Northstar uses to illustrate the problem. Working out whether that one device poses a meaningful risk can mean going through six different tools. An analyst on the platform can type that question in plain language.
In that scenario, the reply shows the laptop belongs to a privileged user who can reach the payroll system. Fixing it then falls to Northstar’s AI agents, which can kick off a remediation workflow to push endpoint protection onto the machine. Humans can supervise those steps where appropriate.

Sin embargo, una propuesta para reformar el RGPD (Reglamento General de Protección de Datos) permitiría que esas empresas entrenen y operen modelos con datos personales sin tener que pedir permiso a cada persona.
Para esto, podrán invocar un 'superpoder' llamado "interés legítimo" y, aunque seguramente algunas Big Tech ya se estén frotando las manos, la propuesta aún no es ley. Veamos de qué va esto.
En corto. El pasado 21 de octubre, un comité llamado Coreper que congrega a embajadores de Estados miembros, acordó la postura con la que el Consejo Europeo negociará con el Parlamento Europeo el Digital Omnibus (un paquete de simplificación de normas digitales). El Consejo publicó un documento de 179 páginas en el que exponen modificaciones sobre ese reglamento europeo de protección de datos, la directiva ePrivacy que regula las cookies, el Reglamento de Datos y la directiva de ciberseguridad NIS2.
Uno de los objetivos de estos cambios (como exponen en el documento y como leemos en IAPP) es agilizar los entrenamientos de modelos de inteligencia artificial permitiendo que las empresas puedan usar datos personales apoyándose en un interés legítimo debido a que la IA se ha convertido en un asunto no sólo tecnológico, sino geopolítico en el que la UE no puede quedarse atrás.

Scale AI est une entreprise américaine dont la plateforme Outlier fait travailler plus de 900 000 contributeurs à l’entraînement d’IA, pour des clients comme Meta, OpenAI ou Google. Cinq plaintes l’accusent de pister ces travailleurs, avec des traceurs tiers et une vérification biométrique, en violation du RGPD.
Ces plaintes ont été déposées le 27 octobre en France, en Italie, aux Pays-Bas et en Autriche par noyb, une association de défense de la vie privée, avec Intérêt à Agir, le groupe de recherche DiPLab et Reversing.Works. Derrière ChatGPT, Gemini ou Grok, il y a aussi des personnes qui vérifient et annotent les réponses des modèles, et ce sont elles que ces démarches cherchent à protéger.
Traceurs tiers et vérification biométrique : les reproches de noyb
Sur Outlier, des contributeurs présentés comme indépendants (ce que noyb conteste) rédigent des prompts, classent des réponses ou annotent des données pour Meta, OpenAI, xAI, Google, Anthropic ou le gouvernement américain. Selon l’analyse technique de noyb, des traceurs de TikTok, LinkedIn, Facebook, Sprig (une plateforme d’enquêtes) et Datadog (de l'analyse de données) se chargent sur leur appareil dès qu'ils sont sur la plateforme. Le traqueur transmettrait toutes les quelques secondes l’adresse IP, des identifiants uniques et la page consultée. Et cela concernerait aussi l’activité de l’appareil hors Outlier. El dispositivo carece de internet, cámara y compatibilidad con aplicaciones modernas, pero su legado técnico y comercial todavía genera interés entre coleccionistas y usuarios de tecnología retro en 2026.

El modelo se diseñó como un equipo accesible, resistente y sencillo de operar, sin las prestaciones que hoy se asocian a un teléfono inteligente. Esa combinación de bajo costo y robustez explicó buena parte de su expansión en regiones donde la infraestructura de telecomunicaciones recién comenzaba a consolidarse.

articles.title: El sistema LZB que ha fallado en el accidente de Toledo debería haber sido sustituido en su totalidad por ERTMS-2 en 2026
articles.summary:
El 21 de abril de 1992, España asiste al primer viaje comercial en una línea de alta velocidad. Es el Madrid-Sevilla construido, entre otras cosas, para dar servicio a la Expo 1992 que se va a vivir en la ciudad andaluza. Quedan 11 años para que se abra la siguiente línea de alta velocidad española, el tramo Madrid-Zaragoza-Lleida del corredor Madrid-Barcelona.
Durante esa década se produce un cambio clave en la extensión de las líneas de alta velocidad en Europa. Esa segunda línea, llega ya con el sistema de seguridad ERTMS que viene a sustituir el sistema LZB, instalado en la línea Madrid-Sevilla. Un corredor que estaba siendo modernizado con este sistema generalizado en Europa y cuya implantación definitiva se esperaba para abril de 2026. El accidente de Urda (Toledo) se produce justo durante este proceso de renovación y antes de que se complete del todo.
El ERTMS es un sistema de seguridad que utiliza protocolos diferentes que el LZB. Ambos están considerados como de máxima seguridad pero desde hace tiempo se ha dado la orden desde la Unión Europea de modernizar las líneas al primero de ellos y abandonar el LZB para armonizar todos los lenguajes de seguridad.
Con motivo del accidente ferroviario de Adamuz (Córdoba), en La Vanguardia recogían que en Europa hay hasta 25 sistemas de seguridad diferentes, con 227.000 kilómetros de vías no operables porque no utilizan el mismo sistema de seguridad. Sony Pays $50,000 for the PS5 Hypervisor Bug, Jailbreak Scene Is Not Happy
Sony has seemingly paid a security researcher named Jordy $50,000 for reporting a PS5 hypervisor bug, and it looks like it's the same bug that PS5 Linux developer Andy Nguyen had found earlier and kept to himself. Jordy's HackerOne profile, under the handle 2tonejordy, lists a single resolved PlayStation report worth $50,000, paid through the bug bounty program Sony launched in 2020. He shared the payout on X on October 14, joking that he "can at least buy GTA 6 with this." The jailbreaking community, however, isn't celebrating.
Back in mid-September, Nguyen announced he was walking away from the PS5 scene and his PS5 Linux work, including PS5 Pro support planned for 2027. According to him, he asked the researchers to wait until GTA 6 launched so people could buy the game and still run Linux, and they agreed, only to report it within a day. Jordy's version is a little different. He says he did agree to hold off, but someone else found the same bug with AI a few hours later, so he reported it, and he insists nobody handed him the bug. articles.title: Jedify formally launches Data Agents for building AI analysts in plain language - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Jedify formally launches Data Agents for building AI analysts in plain language
Enterprise artificial intelligence context startup Jedify Inc. today formally launched Data Agents, a product that lets business teams set up autonomous AI analysts by describing the work they want done in plain language.
Data Agents takes on a longstanding limit of business intelligence software, where analysts have to build dashboards ahead of time around the questions they expect people to ask. Generic AI assistants have tried to fill that gap. In Jedify’s telling, those tools end up guessing at what a business means from its raw tables and schemas.
The company’s core product is a context graph that pulls structured data and documents into a single model of how a business works, down to metric definitions and record-level permissions. Data Agents runs on top of it. Because joins and schema mapping are already worked out inside the graph, building an agent comes down to describing the question.
Users decide when an agent runs, whether on request, on a schedule or when a condition they have defined is met. A market that starts to underperform is the kind of anomaly an agent is meant to catch on its own, and Jedify’s deep research engine then works out what most likely drove the change.
Data access is tied to the person asking the question. Anything that user is barred from seeing, even a single row in a table, stays out of the agent’s results. On cost, Jedify claims its agents burn far fewer toke…

articles.title: Virtana lets its AI agents pull in agents from other vendors to work IT incidents - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Virtana lets its AI agents pull in agents from other vendors to work IT incidents
Information technology observability company Virtana today added Agentic Observability Enterprise Management to its platform so its artificial intelligence agents can pull agents from other vendors into an IT incident.
The release goes after a gap left by the way enterprises have adopted AI agents so far. Most enterprise agents have come built into a single vendor’s product, such as an IT service management system. When a failure spreads across systems from several vendors, none of those agents sees the whole outage. Collating the findings still falls to engineers.
With the new capabilities, a Virtana agent that spots trouble can invite other vendors’ agents into the investigation. Any agent that speaks the Model Context Protocol or the open Agent2Agent protocol is eligible, including those bundled with software a company already owns.
Outside agents have been able to query Virtana’s monitoring data since February, when the company released its System-Aware MCP Server. The feed runs to more than 25,000 real-time metrics. Agents called into an incident also get a shared view of how applications depend on the infrastructure beneath them from the System Dependency Graph, which Virtana introduced at the same time. A month later Virtana extended its monitoring to AI workloads.

articles.title: “Tenemos un historial de pérdidas netas”: la frase de Anthropic que pone en alerta a Wall Street
articles.summary:
La salida a bolsa de Anthropic, la primera de un laboratorio frontera de inteligencia artificial, revela cifras que combinan crecimiento y alarma en partes iguales. La compañía facturó 16.000 millones de dólares en los primeros seis meses de este año, pero acumuló pérdidas de 80.000 millones en el mismo período.
En medio de ese contraste, su folleto previo a la cotización, el S-1, incluye una advertencia que ya circula entre inversores: “Tenemos un historial de pérdidas netas y es posible que no generemos ingresos suficientes para alcanzar o mantener la rentabilidad en el futuro”.
Ese párrafo, ubicado en la página 64 del documento, detalla que Anthropic registró pérdidas netas de 1.500 millones de dólares en 2023, 8.300 millones en 2024, 42.000 millones en 2025 y 80.700 millones en los seis meses cerrados el 30 de junio de 2026.

articles.title: Attackers Hijack Dahua IP Cameras in Ukraine Using P2P Access and Auth Weaknesses
articles.summary:
The Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA) has issued an alert warning of unauthorized remote access to video surveillance systems manufactured by Dahua.
"Cases of compromising IP cameras and DVRs with access to the video stream, changing the device configuration and creating third-party accounts have been recorded," the State Special Communications Service of Ukraine (SSSCIP) said in an alert issued last week.
The primary initial access vector used in the attacks is via Easy4IP, a peer-to-peer (P2P) platform that allows users to remotely monitor homes or small businesses by connecting their Dahua IP cameras, NVRs, and DVRs via a smartphone app or web browser by scanning a QR code or entering the hardware Serial Number (SN).
The agency has warned that the serial numbers have a predictable structure containing a 10-character model prefix that's identical for all units of the same device family and a five-character hexadecimal counter that's incremented almost sequentially (e.g., 7K01F36PCA003E8).
This, in turn, allows attackers to guess them at scale through a brute-force attack and identify if they are connected to the cloud without hitting rate limits or lockouts. As a result, all devices with active P2P functionality are at risk even if they cannot be accessed directly via the internet.
"The assumption that the serial number is unknown to anyone is not a reason to consider the device secure," CERT-UA said.

articles.title: OpenAI Compaction Flaw Let Researchers Bypass Hidden Reasoning Protections
articles.summary:
OpenAI's compaction feature, which shrinks a long conversation to save space, could be turned into a way to copy a model's hidden reasoning out in plain text, security firm Xint has shown.
OpenAI's reasoning models work through a problem before answering, and the service normally returns only the raw reasoning as an encrypted item the user cannot read. The method got past the protections OpenAI added in August against this kind of reasoning theft. OpenAI confirmed the problem and fixed it on October 23, according to Xint.
Xint ran the technique against gpt-5.6-sol, one of OpenAI's reasoning models, using math and algorithm puzzles its researchers wrote themselves. The reasoning it pulled out came from those same requests, and Xint did not claim the method could reach another user's reasoning.
Xint says it cannot prove the copied text is word-for-word the model's real reasoning, because it never had the original to compare against. Two cheaper models each repeated the item and produced the same text, which rules out mistakes in the copying step but leaves open the possibility that compaction reworded the text.
Compaction is an OpenAI feature that uses a model to squeeze a long conversation into a smaller, encrypted item that carries the context forward.

Parmi tous les éléments qui ont abouti à cette amende, le tribunal a constaté « une requête manifestement écrite à l’aide d’un outil d’intelligence artificielle ».
Une amende de 500 euros pour recours abusif
Pourquoi le tribunal a-t-il infligé à Marie-Line X une amende de 500 euros ? Tout d’abord, la contribuable bretonne avait déjà déposé une requête similaire, qui avait été rejetée. Ensuite, elle a saisi le tribunal administratif de Rennes sans avoir préalablement adressé de réclamation à l’administration fiscale, une démarche obligatoire dans ce type de litige. Marie-Line X assure de son côté être « de bonne foi », avoir « suivi les indications écrites » du Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) et n’avoir « jamais été informée d’une dette en 2023 jusqu’à la notification ». articles.title: Why native PC ports of console games are suddenly everywhere
articles.summary:
Why native PC ports of console games are suddenly everywhere — Reverse Engineer Anything gives AI agents a unified toolkit, and byte-for-byte checks keep hallucinations in line
The stage was set, all that was needed was a push... from an army of bots.
Over the past weeks and months, it's increasingly commonplace to encounter native PC ports of previously console-exclusive video games, developed with the help of frontier AI models and a new tool named Reverse Engineer Anything (REA). With dozens of titles ported to PC over the past few months, the big questions are: why is this now possible, and what changed?
The better-known conversions like Super Mario Galaxy and Modern Warfare 2 use AI agents, but their handlers mostly still had to interpret results and direct each step of the process. That's now much easier with Reverse Engineer Anything. Although it shows up in many conversations, REA doesn't do the heavy lifting by itself. It's actually a mix between a toolkit and agent harness, wiring together previously disparate tools under one ceiling.

articles.title: AI-Generated Fake Login Pages Are Making Account Takeovers Easier
articles.summary:
Fake login pages are nothing new, but generative AI is making them easier to build and more convincing. Attackers can recreate familiar login screens, impersonate trusted brands and tailor phishing attempts to specific employees or organizations.
Some fake login pages go beyond stealing passwords. They can also capture MFA codes or hijack authenticated sessions, allowing attackers to gain access to corporate accounts even when additional security measures are in place.
How AI is making fake login pages more convincing
Attackers have long used fake login pages to steal credentials, but generative AI makes it easier to create convincing replicas of legitimate authentication portals. From company logos and page layouts to login prompts, these fraudulent pages can closely resemble the websites employees regularly access.
AI also makes it easier to tailor phishing campaigns to specific organizations or employees. For example, attackers can create personalized IT notifications that direct employees to a fraudulent login page using the company's branding and familiar authentication prompts.
These attacks often rely on lookalike domains that closely resemble legitimate web addresses, with subtle spelling changes or additional characters. Combined with realistic login pages and targeted messaging, these tactics make phishing attempts harder to recognize.

articles.title: MIT desarrolla software inspirado en origami para lograr construcciones más resistentes

Investigadores del MIT diseñaron un sistema de construcción modular basado en origami que permite erigir estructuras tridimensionales livianas y extremadamente rígidas sin necesidad de columnas de soporte interior ni equipos pesados de soldadura. El método utiliza bloques de construcción doblados a partir de láminas metálicas planas y un software que traduce diseños arquitectónicos complejos en piezas fáciles de cortar y ensamblar con herramientas manuales básicas.
“Este trabajo demuestra que doblar metal es un método listo para utilizarse en la construcción de estructuras. Podemos hacerlo lo suficientemente grande y resistente como para sacarlo del laboratorio y llevarlo al sitio de obra”, afirmó Neil Gershenfeld, director del Centro de Bits y Átomos del MIT.
El origami tradicional carece de resistencia estructural
El origami en papel es delicado. Hasta ahora, el origami aplicado a la arquitectura tampoco había logrado superar esa fragilidad. Los pliegues convencionales realizados sobre una sola lámina tienden a generar estructuras inestables, incapaces de soportar el peso que exige una construcción real.
El autor principal del estudio, Alfonso Parra Rubio, y su equipo retomaron patrones de teselado desarrollados en la década de 1960 por el artista Ron Resch. En lugar de trabajar con una única lámina de grandes dimensiones y difícil manejo, el equipo del MIT dividió el problema en bloques de construcción individuales más pequeños.

An attacker who gained access to Keystone's website obtained the key that its hardware wallets use to prove they are genuine, the company said in a statement on October 26.
Someone with that key could build counterfeit devices that pass the online check owners use to verify a Keystone. A buyer who trusted a counterfeit could have their crypto stolen, but the incident did not involve owners' recovery phrases or wallet private keys.
Keystone will destroy 18,835 unsold devices that carry the key, and all new devices will get a new one.
Keystone found the unauthorized access on October 20, and its advice to owners depends on when a device arrived. For a device received after that date with the old key, the company said: "Even if such a device passes authentication, we cannot completely rule out the possibility that it is counterfeit."
Owners of such a device should contact Keystone support and use it only after the company confirms it is genuine.
A device delivered before October 20 that passes the check can be considered genuine and used normally, according to Keystone. The company has not said when the attacker first got in.
The attacker exploited a vulnerability in a third-party data monitoring tool used by Keystone's website to escalate privileges, according to the company. That let the attacker obtain customer data and the key.
Keystone blocked the attacker's access on October 20 and has since fixed the vulnerability. It has not said where the key was stored.

Microsoft has fixed a flaw in its Authenticator app for Android that let a malicious app with no permissions pose as a trusted Microsoft app, such as Teams, and collect sign-in tokens for a victim's work account.
Microsoft tracks the flaw as CVE-2026-80097 and fixed it in Authenticator for Android version 6.2606.4246, so anyone using the app should update.
In the researchers' tests, the tokens gave full access to the account's email, files, and calendar. Microsoft says exploitation also needs the victim to complete a sign-in step in Authenticator, and that the flaw has not been used in attacks.
The research comes from Ofek Levin, working through a fellowship program at the security firm Enclave, which published the technical details on October 23, 2026. Microsoft assigned the CVE on September 8 and rated it 8.6 on the CVSS scale, which it labels "Important."
On Android, Authenticator does more than show six-digit codes. It also acts as a broker: when Teams, Outlook, or another Microsoft app needs to sign a user in, it asks Authenticator, and Authenticator hands back a token, a digital pass that proves the user is logged in. Because the broker controls access to the entire account, it should be careful about which app it grants a token to.

Why UK marketers need mobile-grade measurement before AI can deliver on ROI
How AI is leading to weak measurement practices
UK marketers are entering a decisive phase. Digital advertising investment continues to grow, retail media and connected TV are becoming more central to media plans, and artificial intelligence is moving from experimentation into everyday campaign operations. Yet, the basic commercial question has not changed. Can marketers prove that each pound spent is generating measurable value?
General Manager for EMEA at AppsFlyer.
That question is becoming more urgent than ever. IAB UK has forecast digital ad spend to reach £45 billion this year, with mobile accounting for over two thirds of such spend and online retail media emerging as one of the fastest-growing channels. The same research points to measurement fragmentation as a major industry concern, while AI and automation are now reshaping how campaigns are planned, bought, and optimized.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-86950 (CVSS score: 8.8), is an out-of-bounds write affecting CoreGraphics that could result in arbitrary code execution when processing a maliciously crafted file.
Patches for the flaw were released last month by Apple in versions iOS 26.7.1, iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1, acknowledging that it may have been exploited in sophisticated attacks against specific individuals using devices running iOS before iOS 27.

"Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals on versions of iOS before iOS 27," the company said.
iOS 18.7.11 and iPadOS 18.7.11 also address a logic issue in Audio (CVE-2026-65339) that could be exploited by an app to leak sensitive user information and an access vulnerability in CoreMedia (CVE-2026-86990) that could be abused by a malicious app to access the camera without user permission.

articles.title: GoAhead TLS Flaws Allow Revoked Client Certificates and Enable Session Decryption
articles.summary:
The GoAhead embedded web server loaded a certificate revocation list into its default TLS backend but never turned revocation checking on, so a revoked client certificate could still pass login on affected setups.
The flaw is in builds that use the OpenSSL backend with mutual-TLS, where the server checks a client certificate and vice versa, and a revocation list is configured to block revoked certificates.
That is a setup an operator turns on deliberately; a default build does not. GoAhead 6.1.1, released to device makers on August 2, 2026, and publicly published on October 12, fixes it.
GoAhead is a small web server that device makers build into firmware to run management pages on routers, printers, gateways and industrial controllers. Its maker, EmbedThis, says it runs in hundreds of millions of devices.
The flaw was found by Sébastien Féry of FoxIO, who described it and two other TLS problems in a write-up on October 26.
On an affected build, the server loads the revocation list file at startup and reports no error, so an operator who configured it has every reason to think revocation is working. It is not. A client whose certificate was revoked, for example a stolen or retired device, completes the handshake as if the certificate were still valid and gets whatever access that identity allows.
In FoxIO's test against GoAhead 6.1.0 with OpenSSL 3.6.2, a revoked certificate was accepted with issuer checking switched on.

articles.title: ShinyHunters-Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day Turns Out to Be Three Chained Flaws
articles.summary:
The critical Oracle PeopleSoft bug that ShinyHunters has exploited since May is not one flaw but three chained together, the researchers who reported it said this week.
Oracle patched all three under a single identifier, CVE-2026-35273, in June. Its root is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) that reaches an internal management interface because PeopleSoft trusts its own loopback address by default, opening the door to remote code execution without a login.
The breakdown comes from Bobby Gould of the Zero Day Initiative (ZDI), whose team reported the flaw to Oracle.
In its analysis, ZDI said it reported three distinct vulnerabilities across two PeopleSoft components, and that it is working with Oracle to assign a separate CVE to each. As of this week, the one June identifier is still the only one on the record.
CVE-2026-35273 affects PeopleSoft Enterprise PeopleTools versions 8.61 and 8.62, carries a CVSS score of 9.8, and lets an unauthenticated attacker take over the server over the network. Oracle released its fix in an out-of-band security alert on June 10. The flaw is on CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
Attackers were already using it before that fix was in place. Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) attribute a campaign to the group it tracks as UNC6240, better known as ShinyHunters, that exploited the flaw between May 27 and June 9, mostly against universities. articles.title: Tailscale Patches SSH Flaws That Could Let Hacked Devices Gain Root Access on Other Servers
articles.summary:
Tailscale has released version 1.104.4 to fix flaws in its built-in SSH server that could let an attacker reach services and files on other servers that only the root user should be able to touch.
The flaws are in how Tailscale SSH forwards network connections, a job the Tailscale background process carries out with root privileges. To use them, an attacker must already control a device that the network's access rules permit to open an SSH session to the target, with forwarding allowed in that rule.
The flaws come from a report called Tailworm, published days before the fix by Erica Windisch of Cyberdione Labs, who tested released versions of the Tailscale client and the self-hosted headscale control server in a lab.
Tailscale SSH decides who can connect using a device's identity and the network's policy file, not a password or key, so an attacker does not need stolen credentials, only a foothold on a device the policy already trusts.
The flaws "don't allow an unauthenticated attacker to connect to arbitrary Tailscale SSH servers," Tailscale said, and an attacker can still reach only the machines the policy file already allows.
Tailscale SSH's server runs only on Linux and the open-source macOS build; the attacker's own device can be any platform.

articles.title: Why 'never trust, always verify - repeatably' security strategy for AI Agents, starts after login
articles.summary:
Why 'never trust, always verify - repeatably' security strategy for AI Agents, starts after login
Securing AI agents requires continuous verification of actions after login
Modern digital security frameworks were originally built to correct a flawed historical assumption: the belief that if a user or system was inside the company network, they could be trusted implicitly. Over the past decade, the rapid rise of cloud storage, subscription-based business software, and remote working destroyed that network boundary.
In response, our security models shifted focus. We began verifying the identity of the person trying to log in, inspecting the hygiene of their computer, requiring multiple verification steps during login, and continuously checking that they were who they claimed to be.
Chief Information Officer and Global Chief Information Security Officer at Cato Networks.
This model works well when a human is logging in to perform a task. But with the rise of autonomous AI agents, the real security risk no centralized at the login screen. It starts after access has been granted.
An AI agent does not behave like a standard piece of software. It reads a human instruction, pulls context from company databases, utilizes multiple sets of tools, chooses its own digital tools, connects to external software communication links, and triggers complex automated workflows.
Verifying the initial login simply tells you that the agent is officially recognized by your system. It tells you absolu…

articles.title: WhatsApp prepara ‘Organizaciones’, la nueva herramienta para gestionar grandes comunidades
articles.summary:
WhatsApp prepara una nueva función para ordenar el funcionamiento interno de sus comunidades. Se trata de ‘Organizaciones’, una herramienta pensada para que los administradores controlen con mayor facilidad los subgrupos y los cientos de participantes que puede llegar a reunir una misma comunidad.
El hallazgo lo hizo el medio especializado WaBetaInfo, que detectó la función en la versión beta de WhatsApp para Android 2.26.43.1. Según precisó este medio, el desarrollo aún se encuentra en una etapa inicial.
Qué es la función Organizaciones de WhatsApp
Organizaciones es, en esencia, una nueva pantalla dentro de la aplicación. Permite a los administradores visualizar de un vistazo el número total de miembros que integran una comunidad.
Esa pantalla incorpora un botón con la etiqueta “ver todo”. Al presionarlo, el sistema despliega el listado completo de usuarios junto con el detalle de los grupos específicos en los que cada uno participa.
De esta manera, quienes administran una comunidad podrían dejar de depender de revisar subgrupo por subgrupo para saber quién forma parte de cada espacio. La herramienta centraliza esa información en una sola vista.
Diferencia entre comunidades y la nueva herramienta de gestión
Las comunidades de WhatsApp no son una novedad: la compañía las lanzó en 2022 con el objetivo de agrupar bajo una misma estructura a varios subgrupos que compartieran una temática común.

articles.summary:

The move was in response to the service being used to commit and facilitate prolific criminal activity, including "the advertisement of sexually explicit images of minors, the intentional disclosure of nonconsensual intimate visual depictions of adults and minors, and international money laundering designed to conceal and promote criminal conduct," the DoJ said.
Visitors to the "virtualine[.]net" domain are now greeted by a message that states it has been seized by the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation as part of a coordinated operation between international law enforcement agencies and private sector entities, including the Hessen State Police, the National Police Corps of the Netherlands, the U.K. National Crime Agency, OverRIPE, and Lumen Technologies.
According to court documents, Virtualine, which also operated as Secury, Massgod, Spamhouse, Lanedo, and Omegatech, advertised its services to criminals on cybercrime forums, claiming that they can be used for phishing, carding, email spam, and port scanning, with the exception of child content and terrorism activities.

articles.title: Pour ne pas revivre le fiasco de l’IA, Intel s’offre une pépite du quantique à 2,3 milliards
articles.summary:
Après avoir pris du retard dans l’intelligence artificielle, Intel ne compte pas laisser passer la prochaine révolution informatique. Le géant américain a annoncé ce lundi 26 octobre le rachat de Classiq, une start-up israélienne spécialisée dans les logiciels quantiques, pour un montant qui atteindrait les 2,3 milliards de dollars.
Intel semble bien décidé à ne pas reproduire les erreurs du passé. Alors que NVIDIA a largement profité de l’explosion de l’intelligence artificielle, le fondeur américain prépare déjà son offensive sur un autre marché prometteur, celui de l’informatique quantique. Pour accélérer, le géant de Santa Clara vient de signer un accord en vue du rachat de Classiq Technologies, une entreprise israélienne dont les logiciels pourraient devenir une pièce maîtresse de sa stratégie.
Selon Reuters et Bloomberg, l’opération atteindrait 2,3 milliards de dollars, un montant qu’Intel n’a pas officiellement confirmé. Le rachat doit encore obtenir les autorisations réglementaires nécessaires, avec une finalisation espérée au premier semestre 2027.

Packages keep growing too, with TSMC already mass producing CoWoS-L at 5.5 times the reticle limit. Tool lead times have reportedly stretched from three to six months to as long as eight months. articles.title: Cómo dominar el algoritmo de Instagram y multiplicar su alcance
articles.summary:
Instagram no funciona con un único algoritmo, sino con un conjunto de clasificadores que evalúan el contenido de forma distinta según la sección de la aplicación donde aparece. Dominar su funcionamiento exige abandonar la búsqueda de trucos puntuales y comprender un objetivo de fondo: la plataforma mide y recompensa todo aquello que mantiene al usuario dentro de la app el mayor tiempo posible.
A partir de esa lógica se puede construir una estrategia de contenido que multiplique el alcance real, basada en jerarquías de interacción, optimización de búsqueda y estructuras de video pensadas para la retención.
Cómo funciona el algoritmo de Instagram en cada sección
El comportamiento del usuario cambia según dónde navega, y por eso cada sección aplica reglas propias de clasificación. En el Feed y en las Historias, el sistema prioriza contenido de cuentas que ya se siguen y predice cinco acciones: el tiempo que alguien se detiene a mirar una publicación, si comenta, si da “me gusta”, si la comparte o si toca la foto de perfil.
La cercanía previa con una cuenta, medida a través de mensajes directos o búsquedas anteriores, pesa de manera considerable en esa predicción.
La sección Explorar responde a una lógica distinta, orientada al descubrimiento. Ahí Instagram muestra contenido de cuentas que el usuario no sigue, apoyándose en sus interacciones pasadas y en la velocidad con la que una publicación acumula interacciones apenas se publica.

Wednesday, October 28th 2026
Palit Denies GALAX GPU Factory Closure, Continues Business as Usual
Palit issued a statement today to address and dismiss current industry rumors that GALAX GPU factories are winding down. The rumor suggested that GALAX and its European-focused KFA2 brand were experiencing supply issues with NVIDIA. However, Palit has clarified that these reports are inaccurate. As one of NVIDIA's largest add-in card partners, Palit sells a significant volume through its brands. The speculation that GALAX factories are shutting down due to supply problems with NVIDIA would imply a risk to NVIDIA's entire business with its AIC partners, which doesn't make much sense. Palit explained that since Palit and GALAX are now operating under one roof, they share some manufacturing facilities, and GALAX products continue to be sold.
Palit has also confirmed that the company is developing next-generation GALAX Hall-of-Fame (HOF) graphics cards, along with regular GALAX and KFA2-branded GPU models. While the current generation of GPUs remains available, the mention of next-generation GPUs in development is particularly intriguing. articles.title: Anthropic's Unreleased AI Model Chains Flaws Into Working Chrome, Safari, Windows and Linux Exploits
articles.summary:
An unreleased Anthropic AI model found security flaws in Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows, and Linux and chained them into working proof-of-concept exploits, the company said in its latest report.
The exploits were built in the lab after the model was prompted, not seen in any real attack, and Anthropic reported every flaw to the vendor first, so all of them are already patched. One proof of concept opened the Calculator app on a stock Mac running Chrome within seconds of a page loading, with no further clicks.
Anthropic's Frontier Red Team described five chains in a research post. The strongest claim is not any single bug, but that one model found several separate flaws and combined them into a working exploit, something the company says has until now been the work of a few specialist teams. That capability claim rests on Anthropic's own account.
The patches and the fact that Apple and Google credit Anthropic and its Claude model for specific fixes can be verified with the vendors.
What a reader cannot check is how much of each chain the model built on its own. Anthropic says the work needed only "initial prompting" and "little human involvement," but it does not break down what a person did at each step, and it does not name the model beyond calling it an unreleased, internal research model.

articles.title: Escritores de Stanford demandaron a Anthropic por usar sus libros pirateados para entrenar a Claude
articles.summary:
Dos escritores de la Universidad de Stanford, Tobias Wolff y Chang-rae Lee, demandaron a Anthropic en mayo de 2026 por usar sus libros, descargados de bibliotecas piratas, para entrenar a Claude. Rechazaron el acuerdo colectivo de USD 1.500 millones y piden un juicio con jurado, según informó el diario universitario The Stanford Daily.
La demanda, llamada Cruz contra Anthropic, reclama el máximo legal de USD 150.000 por obra infringida. El acuerdo colectivo ofrecía unos USD 3.000 por obra. Los demandantes también piden una orden permanente que impida a Anthropic entrenar sus modelos con esos libros.
Wolff, profesor emérito de Inglés y ganador de la Medalla Nacional de las Artes, dice que diez de sus publicaciones se usaron sin permiso. Según The Stanford Daily, otros autores de la universidad cuyas obras se habrían usado son Abraham Verghese, Daniel Mason, Hayagreeva Rao y Myra Strober.
Qué decidió el juez y qué todavía no
La prensa internacional ha señalado que Anthropic entrenó a Claude de forma ilegal y que un juez así lo dictaminó. Los documentos judiciales citados por Reuters muestran un cuadro más matizado. El caso Cruz no tiene sentencia: lo que existe son acusaciones de los autores, que Anthropic no ha sido declarada culpable de ninguna en esa causa.
El fallo que sí existe es de otro caso, Bartz contra Anthropic. En junio de 2025, el juez William Alsup resolvió que entrenar a Claude con libros fue uso legítimo. Pero también dictaminó que copiar y guardar más de 7 mill…

Finding the fit that balances audio and awareness

articles.title: Critical 16-Year-Old UEFI Flaw Can Run Code Before Secure Boot on Network-Booting Servers
articles.summary:
A critical 16-year-old flaw in EDK II, the open-source code that most hardware makers use to build UEFI firmware, can allow an attacker to run code on a machine before its operating system loads, but only while the machine is booting over the network.
UEFI firmware is the software that runs first when a computer is switched on, before the operating system. An attacker who can reach the machine with a crafted network message during such a network boot can hang the boot, or, with work tailored to the exact firmware build, run their own code before Secure Boot and other startup defenses load.
An attacker needs no password and no existing access to the machine, but does need to reach it over the network during the short window when it is booting this way.
Red Hat and SUSE, which both ship the affected code, rated the flaw as one an attacker exploits from an adjacent network position rather than across the open internet.
TianoCore, the project behind EDK II, published an advisory on October 22 and rated the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, 9.5 out of 10. A code fix exists, but no stable release of EDK II contains it yet, and the advisory still lists no patched version, so most users have nothing to install today.
What the Flaw Lets an Attacker Do
The flaw is a buffer overflow in EDK II's network-boot code, known as PXE. During a PXE boot, a machine loads its startup image from the network instead of from a local disk.

articles.title: Attention, si un proche vous demande de voter pour une enfant sur WhatsApp, ne cliquez surtout pas

La Gendarmerie nationale alerte sur une arnaque WhatsApp qui circule depuis plusieurs jours. Un proche vous demande de voter pour une enfant inscrite à un concours, mais le lien mène à un faux site conçu pour pirater votre compte.

articles.title: Hackers Target Critical Oracle E-Business Suite RCE Flaw Days After Security Patch
articles.summary:
Threat actors are beginning to probe for a newly patched critical vulnerability in Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS), according to threat intelligence firm Defused Cyber.
The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-101767 (CVSS score: 9.8) in the Oracle Application Object Library of Oracle E-Business Suite. It was patched by Oracle last week as part of its Critical Patch Update.
Security researchers Brandon Peterson, Jimi Sebree, and Noah King of Horizon3.ai have been credited with discovering and reporting the flaw to Oracle on July 24, 2026.
"Our Oracle E-Business Suite decoys recorded exploratory exploits against CVE-2026-101767, an unauthenticated SQL injection in EBS's Thin Client Framework servlet that chains to remote code execution, this morning, October 27," Defused Cyber said in an X post.
In an advisory for the vulnerability, Horizon3.ai described it as an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability that could be chained to achieve remote code execution.
"The vulnerability allows an attacker with network access to the affected Thin Client Framework (TCF) servlet to execute SQL as the APPS database user, then run operating system commands as the EBS application account," the cybersecurity company said.
Specifically, an attacker can issue a crafted request to the vulnerable TCF servlet at "/OA_HTML/AppsTCFServer" to run SQL with the privileges of the APPS database user and ultimately enable system command execution with the privileges of the EBS application account.

articles.title: Anthropic pidió a California que los tribunales puedan suspender modelos de IA que sean un riesgo
articles.summary:
Anthropic, la empresa que desarrolla el chatbot Claude, le pidió al gobernador de California, Gavin Newsom, que los tribunales tengan autoridad para bloquear programas de IA que planteen riesgos graves. La petición figura en una carta enviada en octubre, que el medio Politico publicó el 27 de ese mes.
La carta responde a una orden ejecutiva que Newsom emitió el mes anterior. Esa orden plantea, entre otras ideas, procedimientos de apagado de emergencia, conocidos como kill switch (interruptor de apagado), y la presencia de monitores de seguridad independientes dentro de las empresas de IA.
Anthropic propone que los evaluadores independientes puedan informar los riesgos que detecten al fiscal general del estado. Si este concluye que los modelos de una empresa implican un “riesgo inminente de daño catastrófico”, podría pedir una orden judicial para suspender su uso, su empleo interno o su desarrollo posterior.
Los grandes desarrolladores, agrega la carta, deberían publicar informes sobre los riesgos de sus programas al menos cada seis meses. La empresa sostiene que California puede convertirse en modelo para otros estados y en punto de partida de futuros debates de política pública.

articles.title: Apple recorta puestos de gestión en hardware mientras reorganiza sus equipos de ingeniería

Apple eliminó algunos puestos de gerentes de programas de hardware mientras reorganiza áreas de ingeniería y busca reducir niveles de gestión.

L'actualité chez Intel, c'est bien sûr et avant tout Nova Lake, mais ce serait oublier un peu vite que de nouvelles puces Raptor Lake sont en embuscade.
En marge du lancement de la génération Nova Lake, Intel entend effectivement prolonger son offre en matière de processeurs capables de gérer la DDR4. Raptor Lake Next sera là pour ça et de nouveaux indices indiquent que les puces ne sont plus très loin de nous.
Raptor Lake Next pour rester en DDR4

Il faut effectivement savoir que, modernité oblige, les processeurs Nova Lake ne seront en mesure d'exploiter que de la DDR5. Non que la DDR4 soit particulièrement bon marché, mais cette mémoire de génération précédente reste malgré tout plus abordable et c'est ce qui guiderait Intel dans sa volonté de lancer cette gamme parallèle. articles.title: Google Traductor o chatbot de IA: cuándo conviene usar cada opción para traducir textos
articles.summary:
La elección entre un chatbot y un traductor automático ya no depende tanto de la facilidad de uso o de su costo, sino de cuál es más fiable, teniendo en cuenta que hay una gran variedad de opciones, desde la tradicionales como Google Traductor o DeepL o las opciones de IA como Gemini o ChatGPT.
Sin embargo, no existe una respuesta definitiva porque lo que define el resultado es el contexto que se le aporta al sistema, no la herramienta en sí. Un chatbot permite explicar para quién es el texto, algo que un traductor de caja no deja hacer, lo que no implica que no sea útil. Por eso todo depende para qué se va a usar cada opción.
Cuándo conviene usar cada herramienta para traducir textos
No existe un ranking fiable entre servicios, pero sí criterios prácticos que surge de lo que cada uno documenta.
Google Traductor funciona mejor con documentos con formato y traducción sin conexión. Traduce archivos .docx, .pdf, .pptx y .xlsx de hasta 10 MB, con un máximo de 300 páginas en PDF, aunque esa función solo opera desde el navegador del ordenador, no en el móvil.
En la aplicación de Android se pueden descargar idiomas para traducir sin conexión, útil para viajes. Para fotos de carteles o menús, el texto pequeño, borroso o con tipografía decorativa se traduce con menos precisión.
DeepL también traduce documentos manteniendo el formato. La versión gratuita admite .docx, .pptx y .pdf, y la de pago suma .html y .txt, con procesamiento en infraestructura del Espacio Económico Europeo.
